Πόσους γὰρ υἱοὺς φάσκουσι τοῦ Διὸς οἱ παρ᾿ ὑμῖν τιμώμενοι συγγραφεῖς, ἐπίστασθε· Ἑρμῆν μέν, λόγον τὸν ἑρμηνευτικὸν καὶ πάντων διδάσκαλον, Ἀσκληπιὸν δέ, καὶ θεραπευτὴν γενόμενον, κεραυνωθέντα ἀνεληλυθέναι εἰς οὐρανόν, Διόνυσον δὲ διασπαραχθέντα, Ἡρακλέα δὲ φυγῇ πόνων ἑαυτὸν πυρὶ δόντα, τοὺς ἐκ Λήδας δὲ Διοσκούρους, καὶ τὸν ἐκ Δανάης Περσέα, καὶ τὸν ἐξ ἀνθρώπων δὲ ἐφ᾿ ἵππου Πηγάσου Βελλεροφόντην. Τί γὰρ λέγομεν τὴν Ἀριάδνην καὶ τοὺς ὁμοίως αὐτῇ κατηστερίσθαι λεγομένους; καὶ τί γὰρ τοὺς ἀποθνήσκοντας παρ᾿ ὑμῖν αὐτοκράτορας, οὓς ἀεὶ ἀπαθανατίζεσθαι ἀξιοῦντες καὶ ὀμνύντα τινὰ προάγετε ἑωρακέναι ἐκ τῆς πυρᾶς ἀνερχόμενον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν τὸν κατακαέντα Καίσαρα; Καὶ ὁποῖαι ἑκάστου τῶν λεγομένων υἱῶν τοῦ Διὸς ἱστοροῦνται αἱ πράξεις, πρὸς εἰδότας λέγειν οὐκ ἀνάγκη, πλὴν ὅτι εἰς διαφορὰν καὶ προτροπὴν τῶν ἐκπαιδευομένων ταῦτα γέγραπται· μιμητὰς γὰρ θεῶν καλὸν εἶναι πάντες ἡγοῦνται. Ἀπείη δὲ σωφρονούσης ψυχῆς ἔννοια τοιαύτη περὶ θεῶν, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸν τὸν ἡγεμόνα καὶ γεννήτορα πάντων κατ᾿ αὐτοὺς Δία πατροφόντην τε καὶ πατρὸς τοιούτου γεγονέναι, ἔρωτί τε κακῶν καὶ αἰσχρῶν ἡδονῶν ἥττω γενόμενον ἐπὶ Γανυμήδην καὶ τὰς πολλὰς μοιχευθείσας γυναῖκας ἐλθεῖν, καὶ τοὺς αὐτοῦ παῖδας τὰ ὅμοια πράξαντας παραδέξασθαι. Ἀλλ᾿, ὡς προέφημεν, οἱ φαῦλοι δαίμονες ταῦτα ἔπραξαν· ἀπαθανατίζεσθαι δὲ ἡμεῖς μόνους δεδιδάγμεθα τοὺς ὁσίως καὶ ἐναρέτως ἐγγὺς θεῷ βιοῦντας, κολάζεσθαι δὲ τοὺς ἀδίκως καὶ μὴ μεταβάλλοντας ἐν αἰωνίῳ πυρὶ πιστεύομεν.

english: Even if the Jesus who is called Son of God were merely a man in the ordinary sense, he would still be worthy of that title because of his wisdom; after all, every writer calls God the father of both men and gods. But if we also say that he was begotten from God in a unique way, distinct from ordinary birth, and that he is the Word of God — as we said before — let this be common ground with you who claim that Hermes is the Word of God, the messenger from God. And if anyone objects to his crucifixion, that too is common ground with the sons who suffered beforehand, according to your tradition, who belong to Zeus. For the sufferings of death among those figures are not told as similar but as different; therefore, the unique character of his suffering should not be thought lesser. Instead, as we promised, as the argument proceeds we will demonstrate it to be even greater — indeed, it has already been demonstrated, for the greater one is revealed by his actions. And if we also say that he was born of a virgin, let that also be common ground with Perseus. And when we say that he made the lame, the paralyzed, and those born with defects healthy, and raised the dead, we will appear to be saying things similar to what is said to have been done by Asclepius.

greek: Υἱὸς δὲ θεοῦ, ὁ Ιησοῦς λεγόμενος, εἰ καὶ κοινῶς μόνον ἄνθρωπος, διὰ σοφίαν ἄξιος υἱὸς θεοῦ λέγεσθαι· πατέρα γὰρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε πάντες συγγραφεῖς τὸν θεὸν καλοῦσιν. Εἰ δὲ καὶ ἰδίως, παρὰ τὴν κοινὴν γένεσιν, γεγεννῆσθαι αὐτὸν ἐκ θεοῦ λέγομεν λόγον θεοῦ, ὡς προέφημεν, κοινὸν τοῦτο ἔστω ὑμῖν τοῖς τὸν Ἑρμῆν λόγον τὸν παρὰ θεοῦ ἀγγελτικὸν λέγουσιν. Εἰ δὲ αἰτιάσαιτό τις ἐσταυρῶσθαι αὐτόν, καὶ τοῦτο κοινὸν τοῖς προκατηριθμημένοις παθοῦσιν υἱοῖς καθ᾿ ὑμᾶς τοῖ Διὸς ὑπάρχει. Ἐκείνων τε γὰρ οὐχ ὅμοια τὰ πάθη τοῦ θανάτου ἀλλὰ διάφορα ἱστορεῖται· ὥστε μηδὲ τὸ ἴδιον τοῦ πάθους ἥττονα δοκεῖν εἶναι τοῦτον, ἀλλ᾿, ὡς ὑπεσχόμεθα, προϊόντος τοῦ λόγου καὶ κρείττονα ἀποδείξομεν, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ ἀποδέδεικται· ὁ γὰρ κρείττων ἐκ τῶν πράξεων φαίνεται. Εἰ δὲ καὶ διὰ παρθένου γεγεννῆσθαι φέρομεν, κοινὸν καὶ τοῦτο πρὸς τὸν Περσέα ἔστω ὑμῖν. Ὧι δὲ λέγομεν χωλοὺς καὶ παραλυτικοὺς καὶ ἐκ γενετῆς πονηροὺς ὑγιεῖς πεποιηκέναι αὐτὸν καὶ νεκροὺς ἀνεγεῖραι, ὅμοια τοῖς ὑπὸ Ἀσκληπιοῦ γεγενῆσθαι λεγομένοις καὶ ταῦτα φάσκειν δόξομεν.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
excerpts.anf_chapter_title: Chapter 31. Of the Hebrew prophets
english: Certain people among the Jews became prophets of God, and through them the prophetic Spirit proclaimed events before they happened. These prophets, who served as kings among the Jews at various times, acquired the prophecies as they were spoken and preserved them in books, written in their own Hebrew language under the prophets themselves.

When Ptolemy, the king of the Egyptians, was building a library and attempting to gather the writings of all people, he also learned about these prophecies. He sent to Herod, the king ruling the Jews at that time, requesting that the books of the prophecies be sent to him. King Herod sent them, written in the aforementioned Hebrew language of theirs.

However, since the contents of the books were unknown to the Egyptians, Ptolemy asked him again, sending men to translate them into the Greek language. Once this was done, the books remained among the Egyptians until now, and they are everywhere among all Jews. These Jews read them but do not understand what is said; instead, they consider us enemies and adversaries, similarly annihilating and punishing us whenever they can, as you can also be persuaded.

For even in the recently occurred Jewish war, Barchochebas, the leader of the Jewish rebellion, ordered Christians alone to be led away to terrible punishments unless they denied Jesus the Christ and blasphemed.

In the books of the prophets we find it proclaimed and foretold that Jesus our Christ would come, be born of a virgin, grow to manhood, and heal every disease and every weakness, and raise the dead. It was also foretold that He would be envied and unknown and crucified, and that He would die and be raised and ascend into the heavens, and be the Son of God and be called such. It was further foretold that some would be sent by Him to every nation of men to proclaim these things, and that men from the nations would believe in Him rather than the Jews.

These things were prophesied before He appeared: at one time five thousand years beforehand, at another three thousand, at another two thousand, and again one thousand, and at another time eight hundred years; for according to the successions of the generations, different prophets arose at different times.

greek: Ἄνθρωποι οὖν τινες ἐν Ἰουδαίοις γεγένηνται θεοῦ προφῆται, δι᾿ ὧν τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα προεκήρυξε τὰ γενήσεσθαι μέλλοντα πρὶν ἢ γενέσθαι· καὶ τούτων οἱ ἐν Ἰουδαίοις κατὰ καιροὺς γενόμενοι βασιλεῖς τὰς προφητείας, ὡς ἐλέχθησαν ὅτε προεφητεύοντο, τῇ ἰδίᾳ αὐτῶν ἑβραΐδι φωνῇ ἐν βιβλίοις ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν τῶν προφητῶν συντεταγμένας κτώμενοι περιεῖπον. Ὅτε δὲ Πτολεμαῖος, ὁ Αἰγυπτίων βασιλεύς, βιβλιοθήκην κατεσκεύαζε καὶ τὰ πάντων ἀνθρώπων συγγράμματα συνάγειν ἐπειράθη, πυθόμενος καὶ περὶ τῶν προφητειῶν τούτων, προσέπεμψε τῷ τῶν Ἰουδαίων τότε βασιλεύοντι Ἡρώδῃ ἀξιῶν διαπεμφθῆναι αὐτῷ τὰς βίβλους τῶν προφητειῶν. Καὶ ὁ μὲν βασιλεὺς Ἡρώδης τῇ προειρημένῃ ἑβραΐδι αὐτῶν φωνῇ γεγραμμένας διεπέμψατο. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ οὐκ ἦν γνώριμα τὰ ἐν αὐταῖς γεγραμμένα τοῖς Αἰγυπτίοις, πάλιν αὐτὸν ἠξίωσε πέμψας τοὺς μεταβαλοῦντας αὐτὰς εἰς τὴν ἑλλάδα φωνὴν ἀθρώπους ἀποστεῖλαι. Καὶ τούτου γενομένου ἔμειναν αἱ βίβλοι καὶ παρ᾿ Αἰγυπτίοις μέχρι τοῦ δεῦρο, καὶ πανταχοῦ παρὰ πᾶσίν εἰσιν Ἰουδαίοις, οἳ καὶ ἀναγινώσκοντες οὐ συνιᾶσι τὰ εἰρημένα, ἀλλ᾿ ἐχθροὺς ἡμᾶς καὶ πολεμίους ἡγοῦνται, ὁμοίως ὑμῖν ἀναιροῦντες καὶ κολάζοντες ἡμᾶς ὁπόταν δύνωνται, ὡς καὶ πεισθῆναι δύνασθε. Καὶ γὰρ ἐν τῷ νῦν γεγενημένῳ ἰουδαϊκῷ πολέμῳ Βαρχωχέβας, ὁ τῆς Ἰουδαίων ἀποστάσεως ἀρχηγέτης, Χριστιανοὺς μόνους εἰς τιμωρίας δεινάς, εἰ μὴ ἀρνοῖντο Ἰησοῦν τὸν Χριστὸν καὶ βλασφημοῖεν, ἐκέλευεν ἀπάγεσθαι. Ἐν δὴ ταῖς τῶν προφητῶν βίβλοις εὕρομεν προκηρυσσόμενον παραγινόμενον, γεννώμενον διὰ παρθένου, καὶ ἀνδρούμενον καὶ θεραπεύοντα πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν καὶ νεκροὺς ἀνεγείροντα, καὶ φθονούμενον καὶ ἀγνοούμενον καὶ σταυρούμενον Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἡμέτερον Χριστόν, καὶ ἀποθνήσκοντα καὶ ἀνεγειρόμενον καὶ εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀνερχόμενον, καὶ υἱὸν θεοῦ ὄντα καὶ κεκλημένον, καί τινας πεμπομένους ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ εἰς πᾶν γένος ἀνθρώπων κηρύξοντας ταῦτα, καὶ τοὺς ἐξ ἐθνῶν ἀνθρώπους μᾶλλον αὐτᾷ πιστεύειν. Προεφητεύθη δέ, πρὶν ἢ φανῆναι αὐτόν, ἔτεσι ποτὲ μὲν πεντακισχιλίοις, ποτὲ δὲ τρισχιλίοις, ποτὲ δὲ δισχιλίοις, καὶ πάλιν χιλίοις καὶ ἄλλοτε ὀκτακοσίοις· κατὰ γὰρ τὰς διαδοχὰς τῶν γενῶν ἕτεροι καὶ ἕτεροι ἐγένοντο προφῆται.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
excerpts.anf_chapter_title: Chapter 32. Christ predicted by Moses
english: Moses, the first of the prophets, spoke these exact words: "A ruler will not cease from Judah, nor a leader from his loins, until the one for whom it is reserved arrives; he will be the expectation of nations, tying his donkey colt to a vine and washing his robe in the blood of grapes" (Genesis 49:10). You, therefore, must carefully examine and determine up to what point the Jews had a ruler and king of their own; the answer extends to the appearance of Jesus Christ, our teacher and the interpreter of the unknown prophecies. The divine, holy, prophetic Spirit foretold through Moses that a ruler would not cease from the Jews until the one for whom the kingdom is reserved would come. Judah was the forefather of the Jews, and from him they received their name; after Christ's manifestation, you assumed rule over the Jews and took possession of their entire land. The declaration "He will be the expectation of nations" signaled that all nations would await his return, a fact you can now witness and verify by its fulfillment; people from every nation now expect the one who was crucified in Judea, after whose death the land of the Jews was immediately handed over to you. The phrase "Tying his donkey colt to a vine and washing his robe in the blood of grapes" was a symbolic forecast of what would happen to Christ and what he would accomplish. A donkey's colt stood tied to a vine at a village entrance; Jesus ordered his acquaintances to bring it to him, he mounted it, rode into Jerusalem, where the Jews' greatest temple stood — later destroyed by you — and shortly afterward he was crucified, so that the remainder of the prophecy might be fulfilled. The statement "Washing his robe in the blood of grapes" foretold the passion he would endure, cleansing through his blood those who believe in him. The robe, spoken of by the divine Spirit through the prophet, represents the believers in whom the seed from God, the Word, dwells. The mention of the blood of grapes signifies that the one who appeared possesses blood, yet not from human seed but from divine power. The first power after the Father of all and Lord God is the Son, the Word; he became flesh and human, a matter we will address later. Just as the blood of the vine is produced not by humans but by God, so this indicated that the blood would not originate from human seed but from the power of God, as we foretold. Isaiah, another prophet, proclaimed the same truths through different words: "A star will rise from Jacob, and a shoot will spring from the root of Jesse; nations will hope in his arm" (Isaiah 11:1, 10). A bright star has risen, and a flower has bloomed from the root of Jesse — this is Christ. Through a virgin descended from the seed of Jacob, who fathered Judah, the declared forefather of the Jews, he was born by the power of God; Jesse served as a forefather according to the oracle, and stood in the genealogical line as a son of Jacob and Judah.

greek: Μωϋσῆς μὲν οὖν, πρῶτος τῶν προφητῶν γενόμενος, εἶπεν αὐτολεξεὶ οὕτως· „Οὐκ ἐκλείψει ἄρχων ἐξ Ἰούδα οὐδὲ ἡγούμενος ἐκ τῶν μηρῶν αὐτοῦ, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ᾧ ἀπόκειται· καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται προσδοκία ἐθνῶν, δεσμεύων πρὸς ἄμπελον τὸν πῶλον αὐτοῦ, πλύνων ἐν αἵματι σταφυλῆς τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ“. Ὑμέτερον οὖν ἐστιν ἀκριβῶς ἐξετάσαι καὶ μαθεῖν, μέχρι τίνος ἥν ἄρχων καὶ βασιλεὺς ἐν Ἰουδαίοις ἴδιος αὐτῶν· μέχρι τῆς φανερώσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ ἡμετέρου διδασκάλου καὶ τῶν ἀγνοουμένων προφητειῶν ἐξηγητοῦ, ὡς προεῤῥέθη ὑπὸ τοῦ θείου ἁγίου προφητικοῦ πνεύματος διὰ τοῦ Μωϋσέως μὴ ἐκλείψειν ἄρχοντα ἀπὸ Ἰουδαίων, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ᾧ ἀπόκειται τὸ βασίλειον. Ἰούδας γὰρ προπάτωρ Ἰουδαίων, ἀφ᾿ οὗ καὶ τὸ Ἰουδαῖοι καλεῖσθαι ἐσχήκασι· καὶ ὑμεῖς μετὰ τὴν γενομένην αὐτοῦ φανέρωσιν καὶ Ἰουδαίων ἐβαλισεύσατε καὶ τῆς ἐκείνων πάσης γῆς ἐκρατήσατε. Τὸ δὲ „Αὐτὸς ἔσται προσδοκία ἐθνῶν“ μηνυτικὸν ἦν, ὅτι ἐκ πάντων τῶν ἐθνῶν προσδοκήσουσιν αὐτὸν πάλιν παραγενησόμενον, ὅπερ ὄψει ὑμῖν πάρεστιν ἰδεῖν καὶ ἔργῳ πεισθῆναι· ἐκ πάντων γὰρ γενῶν ἀνθρώπων προσδοκῶσι τὸν ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ σταυρωθέντα, μεθ᾿ ὃν εὐθὺς δοριάλωτος ὑμῖν ἡ γῆ Ἰουδαίων παρεδόθη. Τὸ δὲ „Δεσμεύων πρὸς ἄμπελον τὸν πῶλον αὐτοῦ καὶ πλύνων τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ ἐν αἵματι σταφυλῆς“ σύμβολον δηλωτικὸν ἦν τῶν γενησομένων τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ τῶν ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ πραχθησομένων. Πῶλος γάρ τις ὄνου εἱστήκει ἔν τινι εἰσόδῳ κώμης πρὸς ἄμπελον δεδεμένος, ὃν ἐκέλευσεν ἀγαγεῖν αὐτῷ τότε τοὺς γνωρίμους αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀχθέντος ἐπιβὰς ἐκάθισε καὶ εἰσελήλυθεν εἰς τὰ Ἱεροσόλυμα, ἔνθα τὸ μέγιστον ἱερὸν ἦν Ἰουδαίων, ὃ ὑφ᾿ ὑμῶν ὕστερον κατεστράφη· καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐσταυρώθη, ὅπως τὸ λεῖπον τῆς προφητείας συντελεσθῇ. Τὸ γὰρ „Πλύνων τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ ἔν αἵματι σταφυλῆς“ προαγγελτικὸν ἦν τοῦ πάθους, οὗ πάσχειν ἔμελλε δι᾿ αἵματος καθαίρων τοὺς πιστεύοντας αὐτῷ. Ἡ γὰρ κεκλημένη ὑπὸ τοῦ θείου πνεύματος διὰ τοῦ προφήτου στολὴ οἱ πιστεύοντες αὐτῷ εἰσιν ἄνθρωποι, ἐν οἷς οἰκεῖ τὸ παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ σπέρμα, ὁ λόγος. Τὸ δὲ εἰρημένον αἷμα τῆς σταφυλῆς σημναντικὸν τοῦ ἔχειν μὲν αἷμα τὸν φανησόμενον, ἀλλ᾿ οὐκ ἐξ ἀνθρωπείου σπέρματος ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ θείας δυνάμεως. Ἡ δὲ πρώτη δύναμις μετὰ τὸν πατέρα πάντων καὶ δεσπότην θεὸν καὶ υἱὸς ὁ λόγος ἐστίν· ὃς τίνα τρόπον σαρκοποιηθεὶς ἄνθρωπος γέγονεν, ἐν τοῖς ἑξῆς ἐροῦμεν. Ὃν τρόπον γὰρ τὸ τῆς ἀμπέλου αἷμα οὐκ ἄνθρωπος πεποίηκεν ἀλλ᾿ ὁ θεός, οὕτως καὶ τοῦτο ἐμηνύετο οὐκ ἐξ ἀνθρωπείου σπέρματος γενήσεσθαι τὸ αἷμα ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ δυνάμεως θεοῦ, ὡς προέφημεν. Καὶ Ἡσαΐας δέ, ἄλλος προφήτης, τὰ αὐτὰ δι᾿ ἄλλων ῥήσεων προφητεύων οὕτως εἶπεν· „Ἀνατελεῖ ἄστρον ἐξ Ἰακώβ, καὶ ἄνθος ἀναβήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς ῥίζης Ἰεσσαί· καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν βραχίονα αὐτοῦ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν“. Ἄστρον δὲ φωτεινὸν ἀνέτειλε, καὶ ἄνθος ἀνέβη ἀπὸ τῆς ῥίζης Ἰεσσαί, οὗτος ὁ Χριστός. Διὰ γὰρ παρθένου τῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ σπέρματος Ἰακώβ, τοῦ γενομένου πατρὸς Ἰούδα, τοῦ δεδηλωμένου Ἰουδαίων πατρός, διὰ δυνάμεως θεοῦ ἀπεκυήθη· καὶ Ἰεσσαὶ προπάτωρ μὲν κατὰ τὸ λόγιον γεγένηται, τοῦ δὲ Ἰακὼβ καὶ τοῦ Ἰούδα κατὰ γένους διαδοχὴν υἱὸς ὑπῆρχεν.

english: Moses, the first of the prophets, spoke these exact words: "A ruler will not cease from Judah, nor a leader from his line, until the one to whom it is reserved arrives; and he will be the expectation of the nations, tethering his colt to a vine and washing his robe in the blood of the grape" (Genesis 49:10). It is your task to examine carefully and learn until what time the Jews had a ruler and king of their own; that time lasted until the appearance of Jesus Christ, our teacher and the interpreter of the obscure prophecies, just as the divine Holy Spirit foretold through Moses that a ruler would not cease from the Jews until the one to whom the kingdom is reserved should come. For Judah was the forefather of the Jews, and from him they received the very name 'Jews'; and after his manifestation you ruled the Jews and seized possession of all their land. The statement "He will be the expectation of the nations" was a sign that all nations would await his return, and you now have the opportunity to witness this and be convinced by the fact itself; for people from every nation expect the one who was crucified in Judea, after whose death the land of the Jews was immediately handed over to you as a conquered territory.

The phrase "Tethering his colt to a vine and washing his robe in the blood of the grape" was a symbolic declaration of what would happen to Christ and what he would accomplish. A certain donkey's colt stood tied to a vine at a village entrance; he ordered his acquaintances to bring it to him, and when it was brought he mounted it, sat upon it, and entered Jerusalem, where the great temple of the Jews stood, which you later destroyed; and after these things he was crucified, so that the rest of the prophecy might be fulfilled. For the words "Washing his robe in the blood of the grape" foretold the passion he would endure, cleansing those who believe in him through his blood. The robe, spoken of by the divine Spirit through the prophet, represents the people who believe in him, in whom the seed from God, the Word, dwells. The mentioned blood of the grape signifies that the one who appeared possesses blood, yet not from human seed but from divine power. The first power after the Father of all and Lord God is the Word, the Son; who, having become flesh, became a man — a matter we will discuss later. For just as the blood of the grape is not produced by a human but by God, so it was indicated that his blood would not come from human seed but from the power of God, as we foretold.

And Isaiah, another prophet, prophesying the same things through different words, declared: "A star will rise from Jacob, and a shoot will spring from the root of Jesse; and the nations will hope in his arm" (Isaiah 11:1). A bright star has risen, and a flower has bloomed from the root of Jesse — this is the Christ. For through a virgin descended from the seed of Jacob, who became the father of Judah, who was designated the father of the Jews, he was born by the power of God; and Jesse became a forefather according to the oracle, while also standing as a son in the line of descent from Jacob and Judah.

greek: Μωϋσῆς μὲν οὖν, πρῶτος τῶν προφητῶν γενόμενος, εἶπεν αὐτολεξεὶ οὕτως· „Οὐκ ἐκλείψει ἄρχων ἐξ Ἰούδα οὐδὲ ἡγούμενος ἐκ τῶν μηρῶν αὐτοῦ, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ᾧ ἀπόκειται· καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται προσδοκία ἐθνῶν, δεσμεύων πρὸς ἄμπελον τὸν πῶλον αὐτοῦ, πλύνων ἐν αἵματι σταφυλῆς τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ“. Ὑμέτερον οὖν ἐστιν ἀκριβῶς ἐξετάσαι καὶ μαθεῖν, μέχρι τίνος ἥν ἄρχων καὶ βασιλεὺς ἐν Ἰουδαίοις ἴδιος αὐτῶν· μέχρι τῆς φανερώσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ ἡμετέρου διδασκάλου καὶ τῶν ἀγνοουμένων προφητειῶν ἐξηγητοῦ, ὡς προεῤῥέθη ὑπὸ τοῦ θείου ἁγίου προφητικοῦ πνεύματος διὰ τοῦ Μωϋσέως μὴ ἐκλείψειν ἄρχοντα ἀπὸ Ἰουδαίων, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ᾧ ἀπόκειται τὸ βασίλειον. Ἰούδας γὰρ προπάτωρ Ἰουδαίων, ἀφ᾿ οὗ καὶ τὸ Ἰουδαῖοι καλεῖσθαι ἐσχήκασι· καὶ ὑμεῖς μετὰ τὴν γενομένην αὐτοῦ φανέρωσιν καὶ Ἰουδαίων ἐβαλισεύσατε καὶ τῆς ἐκείνων πάσης γῆς ἐκρατήσατε. Τὸ δὲ „Αὐτὸς ἔσται προσδοκία ἐθνῶν“ μηνυτικὸν ἦν, ὅτι ἐκ πάντων τῶν ἐθνῶν προσδοκήσουσιν αὐτὸν πάλιν παραγενησόμενον, ὅπερ ὄψει ὑμῖν πάρεστιν ἰδεῖν καὶ ἔργῳ πεισθῆναι· ἐκ πάντων γὰρ γενῶν ἀνθρώπων προσδοκῶσι τὸν ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ σταυρωθέντα, μεθ᾿ ὃν εὐθὺς δοριάλωτος ὑμῖν ἡ γῆ Ἰουδαίων παρεδόθη. Τὸ δὲ „Δεσμεύων πρὸς ἄμπελον τὸν πῶλον αὐτοῦ καὶ πλύνων τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ ἐν αἵματι σταφυλῆς“ σύμβολον δηλωτικὸν ἦν τῶν γενησομένων τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ τῶν ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ πραχθησομένων. Πῶλος γάρ τις ὄνου εἱστήκει ἔν τινι εἰσόδῳ κώμης πρὸς ἄμπελον δεδεμένος, ὃν ἐκέλευσεν ἀγαγεῖν αὐτῷ τότε τοὺς γνωρίμους αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀχθέντος ἐπιβὰς ἐκάθισε καὶ εἰσελήλυθεν εἰς τὰ Ἱεροσόλυμα, ἔνθα τὸ μέγιστον ἱερὸν ἦν Ἰουδαίων, ὃ ὑφ᾿ ὑμῶν ὕστερον κατεστράφη· καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐσταυρώθη, ὅπως τὸ λεῖπον τῆς προφητείας συντελεσθῇ. Τὸ γὰρ „Πλύνων τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ ἔν αἵματι σταφυλῆς“ προαγγελτικὸν ἦν τοῦ πάθους, οὗ πάσχειν ἔμελλε δι᾿ αἵματος καθαίρων τοὺς πιστεύοντας αὐτῷ. Ἡ γὰρ κεκλημένη ὑπὸ τοῦ θείου πνεύματος διὰ τοῦ προφήτου στολὴ οἱ πιστεύοντες αὐτῷ εἰσιν ἄνθρωποι, ἐν οἷς οἰκεῖ τὸ παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ σπέρμα, ὁ λόγος. Τὸ δὲ εἰρημένον αἷμα τῆς σταφυλῆς σημναντικὸν τοῦ ἔχειν μὲν αἷμα τὸν φανησόμενον, ἀλλ᾿ οὐκ ἐξ ἀνθρωπείου σπέρματος ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ θείας δυνάμεως. Ἡ δὲ πρώτη δύναμις μετὰ τὸν πατέρα πάντων καὶ δεσπότην θεὸν καὶ υἱὸς ὁ λόγος ἐστίν· ὃς τίνα τρόπον σαρκοποιηθεὶς ἄνθρωπος γέγονεν, ἐν τοῖς ἑξῆς ἐροῦμεν. Ὃν τρόπον γὰρ τὸ τῆς ἀμπέλου αἷμα οὐκ ἄνθρωπος πεποίηκεν ἀλλ᾿ ὁ θεός, οὕτως καὶ τοῦτο ἐμηνύετο οὐκ ἐξ ἀνθρωπείου σπέρματος γενήσεσθαι τὸ αἷμα ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ δυνάμεως θεοῦ, ὡς προέφημεν. Καὶ Ἡσαΐας δέ, ἄλλος προφήτης, τὰ αὐτὰ δι᾿ ἄλλων ῥήσεων προφητεύων οὕτως εἶπεν· „Ἀνατελεῖ ἄστρον ἐξ Ἰακώβ, καὶ ἄνθος ἀναβήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς ῥίζης Ἰεσσαί· καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν βραχίονα αὐτοῦ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν“. Ἄστρον δὲ φωτεινὸν ἀνέτειλε, καὶ ἄνθος ἀνέβη ἀπὸ τῆς ῥίζης Ἰεσσαί, οὗτος ὁ Χριστός. Διὰ γὰρ παρθένου τῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ σπέρματος Ἰακώβ, τοῦ γενομένου πατρὸς Ἰούδα, τοῦ δεδηλωμένου Ἰουδαίων πατρός, διὰ δυνάμεως θεοῦ ἀπεκυήθη· καὶ Ἰεσσαὶ προπάτωρ μὲν κατὰ τὸ λόγιον γεγένηται, τοῦ δὲ Ἰακὼβ καὶ τοῦ Ἰούδα κατὰ γένους διαδοχὴν υἱὸς ὑπῆρχεν.

english: Once more, listen: as He Himself declared, Isaiah prophesied that He would be born of a virgin (Isaiah 7:14). The prophecy runs: "Behold, the virgin will have in her womb and will bear a son, and they will call his name Emmanuel, which is God with us." God foretold through the prophetic Spirit precisely those things that seemed unbelievable and impossible to human beings, so that when they come to pass they may not be disbelieved but believed because they were foretold. We will now try to clarify the words, lest anyone, failing to understand the stated prophecy, accuse us of the very thing we charged against the poets — that Zeus came to women for the sake of lust. The phrase "Behold, the virgin will have in her womb" means that the virgin conceived without intercourse; for if she had intercourse with anyone, she would no longer be a virgin. Instead, the power of God came upon the virgin, overshadowed her, and made her pregnant while she remained a virgin. The angel of God sent to the virgin at that time announced the good news to her, saying: "Behold, you will conceive in your womb from the Holy Spirit and bear a son, and he will be called the Son of the Most High, and you will call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins." Those who remembered all things concerning our Savior Jesus Christ taught this, and we believed them, since even through Isaiah, the prophet previously mentioned, the prophetic Spirit said that He would be born in this way, as we have foretold. The Spirit, therefore, and the power from God are not to be understood as anything other than the Word, who is also the Firstborn of God, as Moses, the previously mentioned prophet, foretold; and this Word, coming upon the virgin and overshadowing her, not through intercourse but through power, made her pregnant. The name Jesus, in the Hebrew language, means Savior in the Greek dialect. From this the angel said to the virgin: "And you will call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins." Since the prophets prophesy carrying no other god but the divine Word, you also, as I suppose, will agree.

greek: Καὶ πάλιν ὡς αὐτολεξεὶ διὰ παρθένου μὲν τεχθησόμενος διὰ τοῦ Ἡσαΐου προεφητεύθη, ἀκούσατε. Ἐλέχθη δὲ οὕτως· „Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει καὶ τέξεται υἱόν, καὶ ἐροῦσιν ἐπὶ τᾷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ Μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν ὁ θεός“. Ἃ γὰρ ἦν ἄπιστα καὶ ἀδύνατα νομιζόμενα παρὰ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις γενήσεσθαι, ταῦτα ὁ θεὸς προεμήνυσε διὰ τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος μέλλειν γίνεσθαι, ἵνα ὅταν γένηται μὴ ἀπιστηθῇ, ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ τοῦ προειρῆσθαι πιστευθῇ. Ὅπως δὲ μή τινες, μὴ νοήσαντες τὴν δεδηλωμένην προφητείαν, ἐγκαλέσωσιν ἡμῖν ἅπερ ἐνεκαλέσαμεν τοῖς ποιηταῖς, εἰποῦσιν ἀφροδισίων χάριν ἐληλυθέναι ἐπὶ γυναῖκας τὸν Δία, διασαφῆσαι τοὺς λόγους πειρασόμεθα. Τὸ οὖν „Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει“ σημαίνει οὐ συνουσιασθεῖσαν τὴν παρθένον συλλαβεῖν· εἰ γὰρ ἐσυνουσιάσθη ὑπὸ ὁτουοῦν, οὐκ ἔτι ἦν παρθένος· ἀλλὰ δύναμις θεοῦ ἐπελθοῦσα τῇ παρθένῳ ἐπεσκίασεν αὐτήν, καὶ κυοφορῆσαι παρθένον οὖσαν πεποίηκε. Καὶ ὁ ἀποσταλεὶς δὲ πρὸς αὐτὴν τὴν παρθένον κατ᾿ ἐκεῖνο τοῦ καιροῦ ἄγγελος θεοῦ εὐηγγελίσατο αὐτὴν εἰπών· „Ἰδοὺ συλλήψῃ ἐν γαστρὶ ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου καὶ τέξῃ υἱόν, καὶ υἱὸς ὑψίστου κληθήσεται, καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν, αὐτὸς γὰρ σώσει τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν“, ὡς οἱ ἀπομνημονεύσαντες πάντα τὰ περὶ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐδίδαξαν, οἷς ἐπιστεύσαμεν, ἐπειδὴ καὶ διὰ Ἡσαΐου τοῦ προδεδηλωμένου τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα τοῦτον γεννησόμενον, ὡς προεμηνύομεν, ἔφη. Τὸ πνεῦμα οὖν καὶ. τὴν δύναμιν τὴν παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐδὲν ἄλλο νοῆσαι θέμις ἢ τὸν λόγον, ὃς καὶ πρωτότοκος τῷ θεῷ ἐστι, Μωϋσῆς ὁ προδεδηλωμένος προφήτης ἐμήνυσε· καὶ τοῦτο ἐλθὸν ἐπὶ τὴν παρθένον καὶ ἐπισκιάσαν οὐ διὰ συνουσίας ἀλλὰ διὰ δυνάμεως ἐγκύμονα κατέστησε. Τὸ δὲ Ἰησοῦς, ὄνομα τῇ ἑβραΐδι φωνῇ, σωτὴρ τῇ ἑλληνίδι διαλέκτῳ δηλοῖ. Ὅθεν καὶ ὁ ἄγγελος πρὸς τὴν παρθένον εἶπε· „Καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν· αὐτὸς γὰρ σώσει τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν“. Ὅτι δὲ οὐδενὶ ἄλλῳ θεοφοροῦνται οἱ προφητεύοντες εἰ μὴ λόγῳ θείῳ, καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὡς ὑπολαμβάνω, φήσετε.

english: Christ was about to release all other human beings from the moment of his birth until he reached manhood, and this has come to pass; listen now to the prophecies spoken for this very purpose. They are these: "A child is born to us, and a son is given to us, and the government rests upon his shoulders" (Isaiah 9:6); this is a sign of the power of the cross, upon which he took the weight of the cross-beam upon his shoulders when he was crucified, a truth that will become even clearer as the Word advances. Again, the same prophet Isaiah, carried by the prophetic Spirit, declares: "I have stretched out my hands all day long to a disobedient and contrary people, to those who walk in a way that is not good. They demand justice from me and dare to draw near to God" (Isaiah 65:2; 58:2). And again, through another prophet, he says in different words: "They have pierced my hands and my feet, and they cast lots for my clothing" (Psalm 22:16, 18). King David, who was both king and prophet, spoke these words yet suffered none of these things himself; but Jesus Christ was put to the test regarding his hands, crucified by the Jews who opposed him and claimed he was not the Christ. Indeed, just as the prophet foretold, they dragged him away, seated him on a judgment seat, and said, "Judge us." The phrase "They pierced my hands and feet" explains the nails driven through his hands and feet on the cross. After they crucified him, they cast lots for his garment and the soldiers divided it among themselves. You can verify that these things happened from the official records compiled under Pontius Pilate. And since it was explicitly foretold that he would sit upon a donkey's colt and enter Jerusalem, we will cite the words of another prophet, Zechariah. They are these: "Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout aloud, O daughter of Jerusalem. Behold, your king comes to you, righteous and humble, mounted on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a beast of burden" (Zechariah 9:9).

greek: Ὡς δὲ καὶ λήσειν ἔμελλε τοὺς ἄλλους ἀνθρώπους γεννηθεὶς ὁ Χριστὸς ἄχρις ἀνδρωθῇ. ὅπερ καὶ γέγονεν, ἀκούσατε τῶν προειρημένων εἰς τοῦτο. Ἔστι δὲ ταῦτα· „Παιδίον ἐγεννήθη ἡμῖν, καὶ νεανίσκος ἡμῖν ἀπεδόθη, οὗ ἡ ἀρχ(??) ἐπὶ τῶν ὤμων“· μηνυτικὸν τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ σταυροῦ, ᾧ προσέθηκε τοὺς ὤμους σταυρωθείς, ὡς πρωϊόντος τοῦ λόγον σαφέστερον δειχθήσεται. Καὶ πάλιν ὁ αὐτὸς προφήτης Ἡσαΐας θεοφορούμενος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ προφητικῷ ἔφη· ,Ἐγώ ἐξεπέτασα τὰς χεῖράς μου ἐπὶ λαὸν ἀπειθοῦντα καὶ ἀντιλέγοντα, ἐπὶ τοὺς πορευομένους ἐν ὁδῷ οὐ καλῇ. Αἰτοῦσί με νῦν κρίσιν καὶ ἐγγίζειν θεῷ τολμῶσιν“. Καὶ πάλιν ἐν ἄλλοις λόγοις δι᾿ ἑτέρου προφήτου λέγει· „Αὐιοὶ ὤρυξάν μου πόδας καὶ χεῖρας, καὶ ἔβαλον κλῆρον ἐπὶ τὸν ἱματισμόν μου“. Καὶ ὁ μὲν Δαυῒδ ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ προφήτης, ὁ εἰπὼν ταῦτα, οὐδὲν τούτων ἔπαθεν· Ἰησοῦς δὲ Χριστὸς ἐξετάθη τὰς χεῖρας, σταυρωθεὶς ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀντιλεγόντων αὐτῷ καὶ φασκόντων μὴ εἶναι αὐτὸν Χριστόν· καὶ γάρ, ὡς εἶπεν ὁ προφήτης, διασύροντες αὐτὸν ἐκάθισαν ἐπὶ βήματος καὶ εἶπον· Κρῖνον ἡμῖν. Τὸ δὲ „Ὤρυξάν μου χεῖρας καὶ πόδας‘· ἐξήγησις τῶν ἐν τῷ σταυρῷ παγέντων ἐν ταῖς χερσὶ καὶ τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτοῦ ἥλων ἦν. Καὶ μετὰ τὸ σταυρῶσαι αὐτὸν ἔβαλον κλῆρον ἐπὶ τὸν ἱματισμὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐμερίσαντο ἑαυτοῖς οἱ σταυρώσαντες αὐτόν. Καὶ ταῦτα ὅτι γέγονε, δύνασθε μαθεῖν ἐκ τῶν ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου γενομένων ἄκτων. Καὶ ὅτι ῥητῶς καθεσθησόμενος ἐπὶ πῶλον ὄνου καὶ εἰσελευσόμενος εἰς τὰ Ἱεροσόλυμα προεπεφήτευτο, ἑτέρου προφήτου τοῦ Σοφονίου τας τῆς προφητείας λέξεις ἐροῦμεν. Εἰσὶ δὲ αὗται· „Χαῖρε σφόδρα, θύγατερ Σιών, κήρυσσε, θύγατερ Ἱερουσαλήμ· ἰδοὺ ὁ βασιλεύς σου ἔρχεται σοι πρᾶος, ἐπιβεβηκὼς ἐπὶ ὄνον καὶ πῶλον υἱὸν ὑποζυγίου“.

english: When the prophetic Spirit speaks from the person of Christ, it declares: "I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people, to those walking in a way that is not good." (Isaiah 65:2) And again it says: "I offered my back to beatings and my cheeks to slaps; I did not hide my face from the shame of spitting." (Isaiah 50:6) "The Lord became my helper; therefore I was not disgraced. I set my face like a flint, and I knew that I would not be put to shame, because the one who vindicates me is near." (Isaiah 50:7–8) And again when it says: "They cast lots for my clothing, and they pierced my feet and hands. But I lay down and slept, and I rose again, because the Lord sustained me." (Psalm 22:18; Psalm 3:5) And again when it says: "They opened their lips, they shook their heads, saying: 'Let him save himself.'" (Psalm 22:7) You can learn that all these things happened to Christ at the hands of the Jews. For when he was crucified, they curled their lips and shook their heads, saying: 'The one who raised the dead, let him save himself.' (Matthew 27:39–43)

greek: Ὅταν δὲ ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ Χριστοῦ λέγῃ τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα, οὕτως φθέγγεται· „Ἐγὼ ἐξεπέτασα τὰς χεῖράς μου ἐπὶ λαὸν ἀπειθοῦντα καὶ ἀντιλέγοντα, ἐπὶ τοὺς πορευομένους ἐν ὁδῷ οὐ καλῇ“. Καὶ πάλιν· „Τὸν νῶτόν μου τέθεικα εἰς μάστιγας καὶ τὰς σιαγόνας μου εἰς ῥαπίσματα, τὸ δὲ πρόσωπόν μου οὐκ ἀπέστρεψα ἀπὸ αἰσχύνης ἐμπτυσμάτων. Καὶ ὁ κύριος βοηθός μου ἐγένετο· διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἐνετράπην, ἀλλ᾿ ἔθηκα τὸ πρόσωπόν μου ὡς στερεὰν πέτραν, καὶ ἔγνων, ὅτι οὐ μὴ αἰσχυνθῶ, ὅτι ἐγγίζει ὁ δικαιώσας με“. Καὶ πάλιν ὅταν λέγῃ· „Αὐτοὶ ἔβαλον κλῆρον ἐπὶ τὸν ἱματισμόν μου, καὶ ὤρυξάν μου πόδας καὶ χεῖρας. Ἐγὼ δὲ ἐκοιμήθην καὶ ὕπνωσα, καὶ ἀνέστην, ὅτι κύριος ἀντελάβετό μου“. Καὶ πάλιν ὅταν λέγῃ· „Ἐλάλησαν ἐν χείλεσιν, ἐκίνησαν κεφαλὴν λέγοντες· Ῥυσάσθω ἑαυτόν“. Ἅτινα πάντα ὅτι γέγονεν ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων τῷ Χριστῷ, μαθεῖν δύνασθε. Σταυρωθέντος γὰρ αὐτοῦ ἐξέστρεφον τὰ χείλη καὶ ἐκίνουν τὰς κεφαλὰς λέγοντες· „Ὁ νεκροὺς ἀνεγείρας ῥυσάσθω ἑαυτόν“.

english: When, however, the prophetic Spirit speaks of future things as if they had already happened—as it is also glorified in the matters previously mentioned, so that it may offer no ground for objection to those who challenge it—we shall make this clear as well. The Spirit foretells the things that are certainly known to be going to happen as if they had already happened. That one must receive them in this way, attend with your mind to what is said. David, fifteen hundred years before Christ became man and was crucified, spoke the things mentioned before; and not one of those who lived before him, though crucified, gave joy to the nations, nor did any of those after him. But Jesus Christ, who is among us, having been crucified and died, rose again, and having ascended into heaven, reigns; and there is joy among those who belong to him, through the apostles, in all the nations where he has been proclaimed, for those who await the immortality he announced.

Δαυῒδ ἔτεσι χιλίοις καὶ πεντακοσίοις πρὶν ἢ Χριστὸν ὄνθρωπον γενόμενον σταυρωθῆναι τὰ προειρημένα ἔφη, καὶ οὐδεὶς τῶν πρὸ ἐκείνου γενομένων σταυρωθεὶς εὐφροσύνην παρέσχε τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ τῶν μετ᾿ ἐκεῖνον. Ὁ καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς δὲ Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς σταυρωθεὶς καὶ ἀποθανὼν ἀνέστη, καὶ ἐβασίλευσεν ἀνελθὼν εἰς οὐρανόν, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ διὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐν τοῖς πᾶσιν ἐθνεσι κηρυχθεῖσιν εὐφροσύνη ἐστὶ προσδοκώντων τὴν κατηγγελμένην ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ ἀφθαρσίαν.

english: The holy prophetic Spirit taught us these things. Through Moses he spoke to the first man formed, telling him that God said, "Look, the good and the evil are set before you; choose the good." Again, through Isaiah, another prophet, he spoke from the face of the Father of all and the Master God: "Wash yourselves, become clean, remove the evil deeds from your souls. Learn to do good; seek justice for the orphan, defend the widow. Come now, let us reason together, says the Lord. Though your sins are like scarlet, I will make them white as snow; though they are red as crimson, I will make them white as wool. If you are willing and obey me, you will eat the good of the land; but if you refuse and rebel, the sword will devour you, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken" (Isaiah 1:16-20).

The earlier statement "the sword will devour you" does not mean that the disobedient will be killed by literal swords. The sword of God is fire, and its fuel is those who choose to do evil. That is why it says, "The sword will devour you; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken." If it referred to a blade that cuts and destroys at once, it would not have said "will devour." So Plato also, when he said, "The cause lies with the one who chooses; God is blameless," took this from the prophet Moses, for Moses is older than every Greek writer.

All that philosophers and poets have said about the immortality of the soul, the punishments after death, the contemplation of heavenly things, or similar doctrines they drew as starting points from the prophets and were able to grasp and explain. Hence seeds of truth appear among all people; yet they are refuted because they did not understand accurately, as shown when they contradict themselves. Therefore, when we say that future events were prophesied, we do not claim they occur by the necessity of fate. Rather, God foreknows what every human will do, and with him stands a decree to repay each person according to their deeds. Through the prophetic Spirit he declares in advance what will befall each according to their actions, continually leading the human race to knowledge and remembrance, proving that he cares for them and provides for their needs.

But by the working of evil demons, death was decreed against anyone who reads the books of Hystaspes, or the Sibyl, or the prophets, so that through fear they might turn people away from gaining knowledge of the good and keep those who serve them in bondage—a plan they could not carry out to the end. For we approach those writings without fear, and we bring them to you, as you see, for examination, confident they will prove acceptable to all. Even if we persuade only a few, we will have won the greatest gain; for as good farmers we will receive our reward from the Master.

greek: Ἐδίδαξε δὲ ἡμᾶς ταῦτα τὸ ἅγιον προφητικὸν πνεῦμα, διὰ Μωϋσέως φῆσαν τῷ πρώτῳ πλασθέντι ἀνθρώπῳ εἰρῆσθαι ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ οὕτως· „Ἰδοὺ πρὸ προσώπου σου τὸ ἀγαθὸν καὶ τὸ κακόν, ἔκλεξαι τὸ ἀγαθόν“. Καὶ πάλιν διὰ Ἡσαΐου, τοῦ ἑτέρου προφήτου, ὡς ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ πατρὸς τῶν ὅλων καὶ δεσπότου θεοῦ εἰς τοῦτο λεχθῆναι οὕτως· „Λούσασθε, καθαροὶ γένεσθε, ἀφέλετε τὰς πονηρίας ἀπὸ τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν, μάθετε καλὸν ποιεῖν, κρίνατε ὀρφανῷ καὶ δικαιώσατε χήραν, καὶ δεῦτε καὶ διαλεχθῶμεν, λέγει κύριος· καὶ ἐὰν ὦσιν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ὑμῶν ὡς φοινικοῦν, ὡσεὶ ἔριον λευκανῶ, καὶ ἐὰν ὦσιν ὡς κόκκινον, ὡς χιόνα λευκανῶ. Καὶ ἐὰν θέλητε καὶ εἰσακούσητέ μου, τὰ ἀγαθὰ τῆς γῆς φάγεσθε, ἐὼν δὲ μὴ εἰσακούσητέ μου, μόχαιρα ὑμᾶς κατέδεται· τὸ γὰρ στόμα κυρίου ἐλάλησε ταῦτα“. Τὸ δὲ προειρημένον „Μάχαιρα ὑμᾶς κατέδεται“ οὐ λέγει διὰ μαχαιρῶν φονενθήσεσθαι τοὺς παρακούσαντας, ἀλλ᾿ ἡ μάχαιρα τοῦ θεοῖ ἐστι τὸ πῦρ. οὗ βορὰ γίνονται οἱ τὰ φαῦλα πράττειν αἱρούμενοι. Διὰ τοῦτο λέγει· „Μάχαιρα ὑμᾶς κατέδεται· τὸ γὰρ στόμα κυρίου ἐλάλησεν“. Εἰ δὲ καὶ περὶ τεμνούσης καὶ αὐτίκα ἀπαλλασσούσης μαχαίρας ἔλεγεν, οὐκ ἂν εἶπε „Κατέδεται“. Ὥστε καὶ Πλάτων εἰπών. „Αἰτία ἑλομένου, θεὸς δ᾿ ἀναίτιος“ παρὰ Μωϋσέως τοῦ προφήτου λαβὼν εἶπε· πρεσβύτερος γὰρ Μωϋσῆς καὶ πάντων τῶν ἐν Ἕλλησι συγγραφέων. Καὶ πάντα. ὅσα περὶ ἀθανασίας ψυχῆς ἢ τιμωριῶν τῶν μετὰ θάνατον ἢ θεωρίας οὐρανίων ἢ τῶν ὁμοίων δογμάτων καὶ φιλόσοφοι καὶ ποιηταὶ ἔφασαν, παρὰ τῶν προφητῶν τὰς ἀφορμὰς λαβόντες καὶ νοῆσαι δεδύνηνται καὶ ἐξηγήσαντο. Ὅθεν παρὰ πᾶσι σπέρματα ἀληθείας δοκεῖ εἶναι· ἐλέγχονται δὲ μὴ ἀκριβῶς νοήσαντες. ὅταν ἐναντία αὐτοὶ ἑαυτοῖς λέγωσιν. Ὥστε ὅ φαμεν, πεπροφητεῦσθαι τὰ μέλλοντα γίνεσθαι, οὐ διὰ τὸ εἱμαρμένης ἀνάγκῃ πράττεσθαι λέγομεν· ἀλλὰ προγνώστου τοῦ θεοῦ ὄντος τῶν μελλόντων ὑπὸ πάντων ἀνθρώπων πραχθήσεσθαι, καὶ δόγματος ὄντος παρ᾿ αὐτόν κατ᾿ ἀξίαν τῶν πράξεων ἕκαστον ἀμείψεσθαι μέλλοντα τῶν ἀνθρώπων. καὶ τὰ παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ κατ᾿ ἀξίαν τῶν πραττομένων ἀπαντήσεσθαι διὰ τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος προλέγει, εἰς ἐπίστασιν καὶ ἀνάμνησιν ἀεὶ ἄγων τὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένος, δεικνύς, ὅτι καὶ μέλον ἐστιν αὐτῷ καὶ προνοεῖται αἰτῶν. Κατ᾿ ἐνέργειαν δὲ τῶν φαύλων δαιμόνων θάνατος ὡρίσθη κατὰ τῶν τὰς Ὑστάσπου ἢ Σιβύλλης ἢ τῶν προφητῶν βίβλους ἀναγινωσκόντων, ὅπως διὰ τοῖ φόβου ἀποστρέψωσιν ἐντυγχάνοντας τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τῶν καλῶν γνῶσιν λαβεῖν, αἰτοῖς δὲ δουλεύοντας κατέχωσιν· ὅπερ εἰς τέλος οὐκ ἴσχυσαν πρᾶξαι. Ἀφόβως μὲν γὰρ οὐ μόνον ἐντυγχάνομεν αὐταῖς, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὑμῖν, ὡς ὁρᾶτε, εἰς ἐπίσκεψιν φέρομεν, ἐπιστάμενοι πᾶσιν εὐάρεστα φανήσεσθαι· κἂν ὀλίγους δὲ πείσωμεν, τὰ μέγιστα κερδήσαντες ἐσόμεθα· ὡς γεωργοὶ γὰρ ἀγαθοὶ παρὰ τοῖ δεσπόζοντος τὴν ἀμοιβὴν ἕξομεν.

english: We resolve this difficulty so that no unreasoning person may turn away from our teachings by claiming we say Christ was born one hundred fifty years ago under Cyrenius, that he taught only later under Pontius Pilate, and that all who lived before him were unaccountable. We were taught that Christ is the firstborn of God, the Word in whom all humanity shares. Those who live by the Word are Christians, even if the world called them atheists — Socrates and Heraclitus among the Greeks; Abraham, Ananias, Azarias, Misael, Elijah, and countless others among the nations. To recount their deeds or names would be long, so we pass over them now. Therefore, those who lived before Christ without the Word were useless, enemies of Christ, and murderers of those who lived by the Word; but those who live and have lived by the Word are Christians, fearless and untroubled. For this reason, by the power of the Word and according to the will of the Father of all, the Master God, a man was born of a virgin and named Jesus; he was crucified, died, rose again, and ascended into heaven. From all this the intelligent person can understand. Since it is not necessary now to rehearse the proofs of this, we turn to the urgent proofs at hand.

greek: Ἵνα δὲ μή τινες ἀλογισταίνοντες εἰς ἀποτροπὴν τῶν δεδιδαγμένων ὑφ᾿ ἡμῶν εἴπωσι πρὸ ἐτῶν ἑκατὸν πεκτήκοντα γεγεννῆσθαι τὸν Χριστὸν λέγειν ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ Κυρηνίου, δεδιδαχέναι δὲ ἅ φαμεν διδάξαι αὐτὸν ὕστερον χρόνοις ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου, καὶ ἐπικαλῶσιν ὡς ἀνευθύνων ὄντων τῶν προγεγενημένων πάντων ἀνθρώπων, φθάσαντες τὴν ἀπορίαν λυσόμεθα. Τὸν Χριστὸν πρωτότοκον τοῦ θεοῦ εἶναι ἐδιδάχθημεν καὶ προεμηνύσαμεν λόγον ὄντα, οἷ πᾶν γένος ἀνθρώπων μετέσχε. Καὶ οἱ μετὰ λόγου βιώσαντες Χριστιανοί εἰσι, κἂν ἄθεοι ἐνομίσθησαν, οἷον ἐν Ἕλλησι μὲν Σωκράτης καὶ Ἡράκλειτος καὶ οἱ ὅμοιοι αὐτοῖς, ἐν βαρβάροις δὲ Αβραὰμ καὶ Ἀνανίας καὶ Ἀζαρίας καὶ Μισαὴλ καὶ Ἡλίας καὶ ἄλλοι πολλοί, ὧν τὰς πράξεις ἢ τὰ ὀνόματα καταλέγειν μακρὸν εἶναι ἐπιστάμενοι τανῦν παραιτούμεθα. Ὥστε καὶ οἱ προγενόμενοι ἄνευ λόγου βιάσαντες ἄχρηστοι καὶ ἐχθροὶ τῷ Χριστῷ ἦσαν καὶ φονεῖς τῶν μετὰ λόγου βιούντων· οἱ δὲ μετὰ λόγου βιώσαντες καὶ βιοῦντες Χριστιανοὶ καὶ ἄφοβοι καὶ ἀτάραχοι ὑπάρχσυσι. Δι᾿ ἣν αἰτίαν διὰ δυνάμεως τοῦ λόγου κατὰ τὴν τοῦ πατρὸς πάντων καὶ δεσπότου θεοῖ βουλὴν διὰ παρθένου ἄνθρωπος ἀπεκυήθη καὶ Ἰησοῦς ἐπωνομάσθη, καὶ σταυρωθεὶς καὶ ἀποθανὼν ἀνέστη καὶ ἀνελήλυθεν εἰς οὐρανὸν, ἐκ τῶν διὰ τοσούτων εἰρημένων ὁ νουνεχὴς καταλαβεῖν δυνήσεται. Ἡμεῖς δέ, οὐκ ἀναγκαίου ὄντος τανῦν τοῖ περὶ τῆς ἀποδείξεως τούτου λόγου, ἐπὶ τὰς ἐπειγούσας ἀποδείξεις πρὸς τὸ παρὸν χωρήσομεν.

english: We will clear up this confusion so that no one, reasoning badly, turns away from what we have taught by claiming that we say Christ was born one hundred fifty years ago under Cyrenius, that what we say he taught came later under Pontius Pilate, and that all who lived before were therefore unaccountable.
We were taught and proclaim that Christ is the firstborn of God, existing as the Word, in whom the whole human race has shared.

Those who live by the Word are Christians, even if they were called atheists — among the Greeks, Socrates and Heraclitus and those like them; among the barbarians, Abraham, Ananias, Azarias, Misael, Elijah, and many others, whose deeds or names would take too long to recount, so we pass them by now.

Thus those who lived before the Word without it were useless and enemies of Christ and murderers of those who live by the Word; but those who live by the Word, both then and now, are Christians, fearless and untroubled.

For this reason, by the power of the Word, according to the will of the Father of all and Master God, a man was born through a virgin and named Jesus; he was crucified, died, rose, and ascended into heaven — from what has been said at such length, the intelligent person will be able to understand.
But we, since it is not necessary now to argue the proofs of this Word, will move on to the urgent proofs for the present.

excerpts.citation: Justin Martyr — First Apology (Chapter 54. Origin of heathen mythology)
excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
excerpts.anf_chapter_title: Chapter 54. Origin of heathen mythology
english: Those who pass on the myths invented by the poets offer no proof to the young people they instruct, and we demonstrate that these stories were spoken through the deceptive activity of evil demons to lead the human race astray. Having heard through the prophets that the Christ was about to come and that the impious among men would be punished by fire, the demons promoted the idea that many men were born as sons of Zeus, thinking they could pass off the facts about Christ as mere wonder-tales similar to the poets' fictions. This was done both among the Greeks and among all nations, wherever the prophets were most likely to be believed as heralds of the Christ. We will make clear that, although they heard the prophetic words, they did not understand them accurately but imitated the truths concerning our Christ while being led astray. Moses the prophet, as we have said, was older than all historians, and through him, as we previously indicated, it was prophesied thus: "A ruler will not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his loins, until he comes to whom it is reserved; and he will be the expectation of the nations, binding his donkey to a vine, washing his robe in the blood of the grape" (Genesis 49:10-11). Having heard these prophetic words, the demons claimed Dionysus was a son of Zeus, handed down that he discovered the vine, wrote that a donkey is led in the mysteries, and taught that he was torn apart and ascended to heaven. Since Moses' prophecy did not clearly indicate whether the Coming One is the Son of God, whether he would remain on earth riding a donkey or ascend to heaven, and since the term used could signify either a donkey or a horse, the demons did not know whether the predicted figure would lead a donkey as a symbol of his presence or ride a horse, or whether he would be the Son of God or a son of man. Consequently, they said that Bellerophon, a mere man, ascended to heaven on the horse Pegasus. When they heard through the prophet Isaiah that he would be born of a virgin and ascend to heaven by his own power, they advanced Perseus as a counterfeit. And when they learned the words, "The strong one like a giant will run his course," as spoken in the earlier prophecies, they claimed Heracles was that strong figure who traversed the whole earth. When they further learned he was prophesied to heal every disease and raise the dead, they brought forward Asclepius.

greek: Οἱ δὲ παραδιδόντες τὰ μυθοποιηθέντα ὑπὸ τῶν ποιητῶν οὐδεμίαν ἀπόδειξιν φέρουσι τοῖς ἐκμανθάνουσι νέοις, καὶ ἐπὶ ἀπάτῃ καὶ ἀπαγωγῇ τοῖ ἀνθρωπείου γένους εἰρῆσθαι ἀποδείκνυμεν κατ᾿ ἐνέργειαν τῶν φαύλων δαιμόνων. Ἀκούσαντες γὰρ διὰ τῶν προφητῶν κηρυσσόμενον παραγενησόμενον τὸν Χριστόν, καὶ κολασθησομένους διὰ πυρὸς τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων, προεβάλλοντο πολλοὺς λεχθῆναι γενομένους υἱοὺς τῷ Διῒ, νομίζοντες δυνήσεσθαι ἐνεργῆσαι τερατολογίαν ἡγήσασθαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τὰ περὶ τὸν Χριστὸν καὶ ὅμοια τοῖς ὑπὸ τῶν ποιητῶν λεχθεῖσι. Καὶ ταῦτα δ᾿ ἐλέχθη καὶ ἐν Ἕλλησι καὶ ἐν ἔθνεσι πᾶσιν, ὅπου μᾶλλον ἐπήκουον τῶν προφητῶν πιστευθήσεσθαι τὸν Χριστὸν προκηρυσσόντων. Ὅτι δὲ καὶ ἀκούοντες τὰ διὰ τῶν προφητῶν λεγόμενα οὐκ ἐνόουν ἀκριβῶς, ἀλλ᾿ ὡς πλανώμενοι ἐμιμήσαντο τὼ περὶ τὸν ἡμέτερον Χριστόν, διασαφήσομεν. Μωϋσῆς οὖν ὁ προφῄτης, ὡς προέφημεν, πρεσβύτερος ἦν πόντων συγγραφέων, καὶ δι᾿ αὐτοῦ, ὡς προεμηνύσαμεν, προεφητεύθη οὕτως· Οὐκ ἐκλείψει ἄρχων ἐξ Ἰούδα καὶ ἡγούμενος ἐκ τῶν μηρῶν αὐτοῦ, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ᾧ ἀπόκειται· καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται προσδοκία ἐθνῶν, δεσμεύων πρὸς ἄμπελον τὸν πῶλον αἰτοῦ, πλύνων τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ ἐν αἵματι σταφυλῆς“. Τούτων οὖν τᾶν προφητικῶν λόγων ἀκούσαντες οἱ δαίμονες Διόνυσον μὲν ἔφασαν γεγονέναι υἱὸν τοῦ Διός, εὑρετὴν δὲ γενέσθαι ἀμπέλου παρέδωκαν, καὶ ὄνον ἐν τοῖς μυστηρίοις αἰτοῦ ἀναγράφουσι, καὶ διασπαραχθέντα αὐτὸν ἀνεληλυθέναι εἰς οὐρανὸν ἐδίδαξαν. Καὶ ἐπειδὴ διὰ τῆς Μωϋσέως προφητείας οὐ ῥητῶς ἐσημαίνετο, εἴτε υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ παραγενησόμενός ἐστι, καὶ εἰ ὀχούμενος ἐπὶ πώλου ἐπὶ γῆς μενεῖ ἢ εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀνελεύσεται, καὶ τὸ τοῦ πώλου ὄνομα καὶ ὄνου πᾶλον καὶ ἵππου σημαίνειν ἐδύνατο, μὴ ἐπιστάμενοι εἴτε ὄνου πῶλον ἄγων ἔσται σύμβολον τῆς παρουσίας αἰτοῖ εἴτε ἵππου ὁ προκηρυσσόμενος, καὶ υἱὸς θεοῖ ἐστιν, ὡς προέφημεν, ἢ ἀνθρώπου, τὸν Βελλεροφόντην καὶ αὐτὸν ἐφ᾿ ἵππου Πηγασου, ἄνθρωπον ἐξ ἀνθρώπων γενόμενον, εἰς οὐρανὸν ἔφασαν ἀνεληλυθέναι. Ὅτι δὲ ἤκουσαν διὰ τοῦ ἄλλου προφήτου Ἡσαΐου λεχθέν, ὅτι διὰ παρθένου τεχθήσεται καὶ δι᾿ ἑαυτοῦ ἀνελεύσεται εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, τὸν Περσέα λεχθῆναι προεβάλλοντο. Καὶ ὅτε ἔγνωσαν εἰρημένον, ὡς προλέλεκται ἐν ταῖς προγεγραμμέναις προφητείαις, Ἰσχυρὸς ἁ ς γίγας δραμεῖν ὁδόν“, τὸν Ἡρακλέα ἰσχυρὸν καὶ ἐκπερινοστήσαντα τὴν πᾶσαν γῆν ἔφασαν. Ὅτε δὲ πάλιν ἐμαθον προφητευθέντα θεραπεύσειν αὐτὸν πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ νεκροὺς ἀνεγερεῖν, τὶν Ἀσκληπιὸν παρήνεγκαν.

english: The evil demons also promoted Marcion of Pontus, whom we mentioned earlier. He denies the Creator God of all things in heaven and on earth, and he denies the Christ, the Son of God, whom the prophets proclaimed. Now he teaches and proclaims another god besides the Creator of all, and likewise another son. Many have been persuaded by him, and those among us who alone know the truth mock them. They have no proof for the things they say, yet irrationally, like sheep seized by a wolf, they become prey to the doctrines of the atheists and demons. For the so-called demons strive for nothing else than to lead people away from the God who made them and from His Firstborn Christ. Those whom they cannot lift up from the earth they have fastened and continue to fasten to earthly and handmade things, but those who are hastening toward the contemplation of divine things they hinder. Unless such people possess a sober mind, a pure life, and a passionless existence, the demons throw them into impiety.

greek: Καὶ Μαρκίωνα δὲ τὸν ἀπὸ Πόντου, ἁ ς προέφημεν, προεβάλλοντο οἱ φαῦλοι δαίμονες, ὃς ἀρνεῖσθαι μὲν τὸν ποιητὴν τῶν οὐρανίων καὶ γηΐνων ἁπάντων θεὸν καὶ τὸν προκηρυχθέντα διὰ τῶν προφητῶν Χριστὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ νῦν διδάσκει, ἄλλον δέ τινα καταγγέλλει παρὰ τὸν δημιουργὸν τῶν πάντων θεὸν καὶ ὁμοίως ἕτερον υἱόν· ᾧ πολλοὶ πεισθέντες ὁ ς μόνῳ τἀληθῆ ἐπισταμένῳ ἡμῶν καταγελῶσιν, ἀπόδειξιν μηδεμίαν περὶ ὧν λέγουσιν ἔχοντες, ἀλλὰ ἀλόγως ὡς ὑπὸ λύκου ἄρνες συνηρπασμένοι βορὰ τῶν ἀθέων δογμάτων καὶ δαιμόνων γίνονται. Οὐ γὰρ ἄλλο τι ἀγωνίζονται οἱ λεγόμενοι δαίμονες, ἢ ἀπάγειν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἀπὸ τοῦ ποιήσαντος θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ πρωτογόνου αὐτοῦ Χριστοῦ· καὶ τοὺς μὲν τῆς γῆς μὴ ἐπαίρεσθαι δυναμένους τοῖς γηΐνοις καὶ χειροποιήτοις προσήλωσαν καὶ προσηλοῦσι, τοὺς δὲ ἐπὶ θεωρίαν θείων ὁρμῶντας ὑπεκκρούοντες, ἢν μὴ λογισμὸν σώφρονα καὶ καθαρὸν καὶ ἀπαθῆ βίον ἔχωσιν, εἰς ἀσέβειαν ἐμβάλλουσιν.

excerpts.anf_chapter_title: Chapter 63. How God appeared to Moses
english: Even now, all Jews teach that the unnamed God spoke to Moses. Therefore the prophetic Spirit, through the prophet Isaiah whom we mentioned earlier, rebukes them with words we have already cited: "The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's manger, but Israel does not know me, and my people do not understand me" (Isaiah 1:3). Because the Jews did not understand what Father and Son truly are, Jesus the Christ also rebukes them in a similar way, declaring: "No one knows the Father except the Son, nor the Son except the Father, and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal him" (Matthew 11:27). The Word of God is his Son, as we stated before. He is also called an angel and an apostle, because he announces everything that must be known and is sent to proclaim what he announces, just as our Lord himself said: "Whoever hears me hears the one who sent me" (Luke 10:16).

This will become evident from the writings of Moses. For it is written there: "And an angel of God spoke to Moses in a flame of fire from the bush, and said: I am the one who is, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, the God of your fathers. Go down to Egypt and lead out my people" (Exodus 3:2, 6, 10). You can learn what follows from these passages if you wish, since it is not possible to record everything here. Yet these words serve as proof that Jesus the Christ, who existed before as the Word and appeared at one time in the form of fire and at another in an incorporeal image, is the Son of God and the apostle. Through the will of God he became a man on behalf of the human race, and he endured and suffered what the demons, incited by the senseless Jews, brought upon him.

Although the ordinances of Moses state expressly: "And an angel of God spoke to Moses in a flame of fire from the bush, and said: I am the one who is, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob" (Exodus 3:2, 6), they claim that the Father of all, the Creator who spoke these words, is the one speaking. Therefore the prophetic Spirit also rebukes them: "But Israel does not know me, and the people do not understand me" (Isaiah 1:3). And again Jesus, as we have shown, would say to them: "No one knows the Father except the Son, nor the Son except the Father, and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal him" (Matthew 11:27). Because the Jews have always believed that the Father of all spoke to Moses, when in fact it was the Son of God, who is also called an angel and an apostle, they are justly convicted both by the prophetic Spirit and by Christ himself of knowing neither the Father nor the Son.

Those who say the Son is the Father are convicted of knowing neither the Father, nor that he has a Son, the Father of all, who as the Word and firstborn of God exists. Previously, through the form of fire and an incorporeal image, he appeared to Moses and the other prophets; but now, in the time of your rule, as we said before, he became a man through a virgin according to the will of the Father for the salvation of those who believe in him. He endured scorn and suffering, so that by dying and rising he might conquer death.

What was spoken to Moses from the bush — "I am the one who is, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob, and the God of your fathers" (Exodus 3:6, 15) — signifies that even though they died, they remain and are Christ's people. For they were the first of all human beings to devote themselves to the search for God: Abraham, the father of Isaac; Isaac, the father of Jacob; as Moses also wrote (Genesis 12–35).

greek: Ἰουδαῖοι δὲ πάντες καὶ νῦν διδάσκουσι τὸν ἀνωνόμαστον θεὸν λελαληκέναι τῷ Μωυσεῖ. Ὁθεν τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα διὰ Ἡσαΐου τοῦ προμεμηνυμένου προφήτου ἐλέγχον αὐτούς, ὡς προεγράψαμεν, εἶπεν· „Ἔγνω βοῦς τὸν κτησάμενον καὶ ὄνος τὴν φάτνην τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ, Ἰσραὴλ δέ με οὐκ ἔγνω καὶ ὁ λαός με οὐ συνῆκε“. Καὶ Ἰησοῦς δὲ ὁ Χριστός, ότι οὐκ ἔγνωσαν Ἰουδαῖοι, τί πατὴρ καὶ τί υἱός, ὁμοίως ἐλέγχων αὐτοὺς καὶ αὐτὸς εἶπεν· „Οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τὸν πατέρα εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱός, οὐδὲ τὸν υἱὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ οἷς ἂν ἀποκαλύψῃ ὁ υἱός“. Ὁ λόγος δὲ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ, ὡς προέφημεν. Καὶ ἄγγελος δὲ καλεῖται καὶ ἀπόστολος· αὐτὸς γὰρ ἀπαγγέλλει, ὅσα δεῖ γνωσθῆναι, καὶ ἀποστέλλεται μηνύσων, ὅσα ἀγγέλλεται, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς ἱ κύριος ἡμῶν εἶπεν· „Ὁ ἐμοῦ ἀκούων ἀκούει τοῦ ἀποστείλαντός με“. Καὶ ἐκ τῶν τοῦ Μωϋσέως δὲ συγγραμμάτων φανερὸν τοῦτο γενήσεται. Λέλεκται δὲ ἐν αὐτοῖς οὕτως· „Καὶ ἐλάλησε Μωϋσεῖ ἄγγελος θεοῦ ἐν φλογὶ πυρὸς ἐκ τῆς βάτου καὶ εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, θεὸς Ἀβραάμ, θεὸς Ἰσαάκ, θεὸς Ἰακώβ, ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου. Κάτελθε εἰς Αἰγυπτον καὶ ἐξάγαγε τὸν λαόν μου“. Τὰ δ᾿ ἑπόμενα ἐξ ἐκείνων βουλόμενοι μαθεῖν δύνασθε· οὐ γὰρ δυνατὸν ἐν τούτοις ἀναγράψαι πάντα. Ἀλλ᾿ εἰς ἀπόδειξιν γεγόνασιν οἵδε οἱ λόγοι, ότι υἱὸς θεοῦ καὶ ἀπόστολος ᾿Ιησοῦς ὁ Χριστός ἐστι, πρότερον λόγος ὤν, καὶ ἐν ἰδέᾳ πυρὶ ς ποτὲ φανείς, ποτὲ δὲ καὶ ἐν εἰκόνι ἀσωμάτῳ· νῦν δὲ διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἀνθρωπείου γένους ἄνθρωπος γενόμενος ὑπέμεινε καὶ παθεῖν, ὅσα αὐτὸν ἐνήργησαν οἱ δαίμονες διατεθῆναι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνοήτων Ἰουδαίων. Οἵτινες ἔχοντες ῥητῶς εἰρημένον ἐν τοῖς Μωϋσέως συντάγμασι· „Καὶ ἐλάλησεν ἄγγελος τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ Μωϋσεῖ ἐν πυρὶ φλογὸς ἐν βάτῳ καὶ εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, ἱ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακώβ“, τὸν τῶν όλων πατέρα καὶ δημιουργὸν τὸν ταῦτα εἰπόντα λέγουσιν εἶναι. Ὅθεν καὶ τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα ἐλέγχον αὐτοὺς εἶπεν· „Ἰσραὴλ δέ με οὐκ ἔγνω, καὶ ὁ λαός με οὐ συνῆκε“. Καὶ πάλιν ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ὡς ἐδηλώσαμεν, παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς ἂν εἶπεν· „Οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τὸν πατέρα εἰ μἰ ὁ υἱός, οὐδὲ τὸν υἱὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ οἷς ἂν ἱ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψῃ“. Ἰουδαῖοι οὖν ἡγησάμενοι ἀεὶ τὸν πατέρα τᾶν ὅλων λελαληκέναι τῷ Μωϋσεῖ, τοῦ λαλήσαντος αὐτῷ ὄντος υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὃς καὶ ἄγγελος καὶ ἀπόστολος κέκληται, δικαίως ἐλέγχονται καὶ διὰ τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος καὶ δι᾿ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς οὔτε τὸν πατέρα οὔτε τὸν υἱὸν ἔγνωσαν. Οἱ γὰρ τὸν υἱὸν πατέρα φάσκοντες εἶναι ἐλέγχονται μήτε τὸν πατέρα ἐπιστάμενοι, μηθ᾿ ότι ἐστὶν υἱὸς τῷ πατρὶ τῶν ὅλων γινώσκοντες· ὃς λόγος καὶ πρωτότοκος ὢν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ θεὶς ὑπάρχει. Καὶ πρότερον διὰ τῆς τοῦ πυρὸς μορφῆς καὶ εἰκόνος ἀσωμάτου τῷ Μωϋσεῖ καὶ τοῖς ἑτέροις προφήταις ἐφάνη· νῦν δ᾿ ἐν χρόνοις τῆς ὑμετέρας ἀρχῆς, ὡς προείπομεν, διὰ παρθένου ἄνθρωπος γενόμενος κατὰ τὴν τοῦ πατρὸς βουλὴν ὑπὲρ σωτηρίας τῶν πιστευόντων αὐτῷ καὶ ἐξουθενηθῆναι καὶ παθεῖν ὑπέμενεν, ἵνα ἀποθανὼν καὶ ἀναστὰς νικήσῃ τὸν θάνατον. Τὶ δὲ εἰρημένον ἐκ βάτου τῷ Μωϋσεῖ· „Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακὼβ καὶ ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου“, σημαντικὸν τοῦ καὶ ἀποθανόντας ἐκείνους μένειν καὶ εἶναι αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀνθρώπους· καὶ γὰρ πρῶτοι τῶν πάντων ἀνθρώπων ἐκεῖνοι περὶ θεοῦ ζήτησιν ἠσχολήθησαν, Ἀβραὰμ μὲν πατὴρ ὢν τοῦ Ἰσαάκ, Ἰσαὰκ δὲ τοῦ Ἰακώβ, ὡς καὶ Μωϋσῆς ἀνέγραψε.

excerpts.citation: Athenagoras — Plea for the Christians (Chapter 4. The Christians are Not Atheists, But Acknowledge One Only God.)
excerpts.author: Athenagoras
excerpts.locus: Chapter 4. The Christians are Not Atheists, But Acknowledge One Only God.
excerpts.anf_chapter_title: Chapter 4. The Christians are Not Atheists, But Acknowledge One Only God.
english: We are not atheists. I will answer each accusation so that those who speak against us do not look ridiculous for failing to refute us. The Athenians reasonably charged Diagoras with atheism, not only because he published the Orphic story, divulged the mysteries of Eleusis and of the Cabiri, and chopped up the wooden image of Heracles to cook his gourds, but also because he declared outright that there is no god at all. But we separate God from matter and show that matter is one thing and God another, with a great gulf between them: the divine is uncreated and eternal, perceived only by mind and reason, while matter is created and perishable. Do they not unreasonably call us atheists? If we thought like Diagoras, despite possessing so many pledges of piety—the order, the universal harmony, the size, the color, the shape, the disposition of the world—it would be reasonable for us also to have the reputation of impiety and to be despised. But since our reason leads to one God, the creator of this universe, who himself has not come into being (for what exists does not come into being, but what does not exist), and has made all things through his reason that is with him, we suffer unreasonably, and are spoken of badly, and are persecuted.

greek: Ὅτι μὲν οὖν οὐκ ἐσμὲν ἄθεοι· πρὸς ἓν ἕκαστον ἀπαντήσω τῶν ἐγκλημάτων, μὴ καὶ γελοῖον ᾖ τοὺς λέγοντας μὴ ἐλέγχειν· Διαγόρᾳ μὲν γὰρ εἰκότως ἀθεότητα ἐπεκάλουν Ἀθηναῖοι, μὴ μόνον τὸν Ὀρφικὸν εἰς μέσον κατατιθέντι λόγον καὶ τὰ ἐν Ἐλευσῖνι καὶ τὰ τῶν Καβείρων δημεύοντι μυστήρια καὶ τὸ τοῦ Ἡρακλέους ἵνα τὰς γογγύλας ἑψοῖ κατακόπτοντι ξόανον, ἄντικρυς δὲ ἀποφαινομένῳ μηδ᾿ ὅλως εἶναι θεόν. Ἡμῖν δέ, διαιροῦσιν ἀπὸ τῆς ὕλης τὸν θεόν, καὶ δεικνύουσιν ἕτερον μέν τι εἶναι τὴν ὕλην ἄλλο δὲ τὸν θεὸν καὶ τὸ διὰ μέσου πολύ (τὸ μὲν γὰρ θεῖον ἀγένητον εἶναι καὶ ἀΐδιον, νῷ μόνῳ καὶ λόγῳ θεωρούμενον, τὴν δὲ ὕλην γενητὴν καὶ φθαρτήν), μή τι οὐκ ἀλόγως τὸ τῆς ἀθεότητος ἐπικαλοῦσιν ὄνομα; Εἰ μὲν γὰρ ἐφρονοῦμεν ὅμοια τῷ Διαγόρᾳ, τοσαῦτα ἔχοντες πρὸς θεοσέβειαν ἐνέχυρα, τὸ εὔτακτον, τὸ διὰ παντὸς σύμφωνον, τὸ μέγεθος, τὴν χροίαν, τὸ σχῆμα, τὴν διάθεσιν τοῦ κόσμου, εἰκότως ἂν ἡμῖν καὶ ἡ τοῦ μὴ θεοσεβεῖν δόξα καὶ ἡ τοῦ ἐλαύνεσθαι αἰτία προσετρίβετο. Ἐπεὶ δὲ ὁ λόγος ἡμῶν ἕνα θεὸν ἄγει τὸν τοῦδε τοῦ παντὸς ποιητήν, αὐτὸν μὲν οὐ γενόμενον (ὅτι τὸ ὂν οὐ γίνεται ἀλλὰ τὸ μὴ ὄν), πάντα δὲ διὰ τοῦ παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ λόγου πεποιηκότα, ἑκάτερα ἀλόγως πάσχομεν, καὶ κακῶς ἀγορευόμεθα καὶ διωκόμεθα.

excerpts.citation: Athenagoras — Plea for the Christians (Chapter 8. Absurdities of Polytheism.)
excerpts.author: Athenagoras
excerpts.anf_chapter_title: Chapter 8. Absurdities of Polytheism.
english: Consider this, so that you may also share our reasoning for the faith: from the beginning, one God is the creator of this universe. If two or more gods existed from the beginning, either they existed in one and the same reality or each existed separately. They could not exist in one and the same reality; not because they would be similar gods, but because as uncreated beings they are dissimilar. Created things resemble their patterns, but uncreated things are dissimilar, having been made neither from anything nor toward anything. But if, like a hand, an eye, and a foot that are parts around one body and together complete one body, God is one? Yet Socrates, because he is created and perishable, is composed and divided into parts; God, however, is uncreated, impassive, and indivisible, and therefore does not consist of parts. If instead each god exists separately, given that the one who made the world is above the things that have been made and encompasses those things he made and adorned, where is the other god or the rest? If the world, having been completed as a sphere, is enclosed by the circles of heaven, and the creator of the world holds it above the things that have been made by his forethought, what is the place of the other god or the rest? He is not in the world, because the world belongs to another; nor is he around the world, for the creator of the world, God, is above the world. If he is neither in the world nor around the world (for everything around it is held by this creator), where is he? Above the world and God? In another world or around another? But if he is in another or around another, he is no longer around us (for he does not rule the world), nor is he great in power (for he exists in a limited place). If he is neither in another world (for this one has filled all) nor around another (for this one holds all), then he does not exist, since there is no place in which he exists. What does he do, when another reality exists in which the world is, and he himself is above the creator of the world, yet is neither in the world nor around the world? Is there something else so that he may stand somewhere? But God is above him and the things of God. What place will remain, when this one has filled the things above the world? Does he exercise forethought? Yet he has made nothing unless he exercises forethought. If he neither makes nor exercises forethought nor has another place in which to exist, then this one from the beginning and alone is the creator of the world, God.

greek: Ὅτι τοίνυν εἷς ἐξ ἀρχῆς ὁ τοῦδε τοῦ παντὸς ποιητὴς θεὸς οὑτωσὶ σκέψασθε, ἵν᾿ ἔχητε καὶ τὸν λογισμὸν ἡμῶν τῆς πίστεως. Εἰ δύο ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἢ πλείους ἦσαν θεοί, ἤτοι ἐν ἑνὶ καὶ ταὐτῷ ἦσαν ἢ ἰδίᾳ ἕκαστος αὐτῶν. Ἐν μὲν οὖν ἑνὶ καὶ ταὐτῷ εἶναι οὐκ ἠδύναντο. Οὐ γὰρ εἰ θεοὶ ὅμοιοι, ἀλλ᾿ ὅτι ἀγένητοι οὐχ ὅμοιοι· τὰ μὲν γὰρ γενητὰ ὅμοια τοῖς παραδείγμασι, τὰ δὲ ἀγένητα ἀνόμοια, οὔτε ἀπό τινος οὔτε πρός τινα γενόμενα. Εἰ δέ, ὡς χεὶρ καὶ ὀφθαλμὸς καὶ ποὺς περὶ ἓν σῶμά εἰσιν τὰ μέρη, ἕνα ἐξ αὐτῶν συμπληροῦντες, ὁ θεὸς εἶς; Καίτοι ὁ μὲν Σωκράτης, παρὸ γενητὸς καὶ φθαρτός, συγκείμενος καὶ διαιρούμενος εἰς μέρη· ὁ δὲ θεὸς ἀγένητος καὶ ἀπαθὴς καὶ ἀδιαίρετος, οὐκ ἄρα συνεστὼς ἐκ μερῶν. Εἰ δὲ ἰδίᾳ ἕκαστος αὐτῶν, ὄντος τοῦ τὸν κόσμον πεποιηκότος ἀνωτέρω τῶν γεγονότων καὶ περὶ ἃ ἐποίησέ τε καὶ ἐκόσμησε, ποῦ· ὁ ἕτερος ἢ οἱ λοιποί; Εἰ γὰρ ὁ μὲν κόσμος σφαιρικὸς ἀποτελεσθεὶς οὐρανοῦ κύκλοις ἀποκέκλεισται, ὁ δὲ τοῦ κόσμου ποιητὴς ἀνωτέρω τῶν γεγονότων ἐπέχων αὐτὸν τῇ τούτων προνοίᾳ, τίς ὁ τοῦ ἑτέρου θεοῦ ἢ τῶν λοιπῶν τόπος; Οὔτε γὰρ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἐστίν, ὅτι ἑτέρου ἐστίν· οὔτε περὶ τὸν κόσμον, ὑπὲρ γὰρ τοῦτον ὁ τοῦ κόσμου ποιητὴς θεός. Εἰ δὲ μήτε ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἐστὶ μήτε περὶ τὸν κόσμον (τὸ γὰρ περὶ αὐτὸν πᾶν ὑπὸ τούτου κατέχεται), ποῦ ἐστιν; Ἀνωτέρω τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τοῦ θεοῦ; Ἐν ἑτέρῳ κόσμῳ ἢ περὶ ἕτερον; Ἀλλ᾿ εἰ μέν ἐστιν ἐν ἑτέρῳ ἢ περὶ ἕτερον, οὔτε περὶ ἡμᾶς ἐστιν ἔτι (οὔ τε γὰρ κόσμου κρατεῖ), οὔτε αὐτὸς δυνάμει μέγας ἐστίν (ἐν γὰρ περιωρισμένῳ τόπῳ ἐστίν). Εἰ δὲ οὔτε ἐν ἑτέρῳ κόσμῳ ἐστὶν (πάντα γὰρ ὑπὸ τούτου πεπλήρωται) οὔτε περὶ ἕτερον (πάντα γὰρ ὑπὸ τούτου κατέχεται), καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν, οὐκ ὄντος ἐν ᾧ ἐστιν. Ἢ τί ποιεῖ, ἑτέρου μὲν ὄντος οὗ ἐστιν ὁ κόσμος, αὐτὸς δὲ ἀνωτέρω ὢν τοῦ ποιητοῦ τοῦ κόσμου, οὐκ ὤν δὲ οὔτε ἐν κόσμῳ οὔτε περὶ κόσμον; Ἀλλ᾿ ἔστι τι ἕτερον, ἵνα που στῇ; Ἀλλ᾿ ὑπὲρ αὐτὸν ὁ θεὸς καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ. Καὶ τίς ἔσται τόπος, τὰ ὑπὲρ τὸν κόσμον τούτου πεπληρωκότος; Ἀλλὰ προνοεῖ; Καὶ μὴν οὐδέν, εἰ μὴ προνοεῖ, πεποίηκεν. Εἰ δὲ μὴ ποιεῖ μήτε προνοεῖ μήτε ἐστὶ τόπος ἕτερος ἐν ᾧ ἐστιν, εἷς οὗτος ἐξ ἀρχῆς καὶ μόνος ὁ ποιητὴς τοῦ κόσμου θεός.

excerpts.citation: Athenagoras — Plea for the Christians (Chapter 10. The Christians Worship the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.)
excerpts.author: Athenagoras
excerpts.locus: Chapter 10. The Christians Worship the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.
excerpts.anf_chapter_title: Chapter 10. The Christians Worship the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.
english: I have sufficiently shown that we are not atheists, because we acknowledge one God who is ungenerated, eternal, invisible, impassible, incomprehensible, and uncircumscribed, whom mind and word alone grasp, and who is encompassed by light, beauty, spirit, and indescribable power; under him all things have been made through his word and are adorned and held together. We also conceive of the Son of God. Let no one think it absurd that the Son belongs to God. We have not thought about God the Father or about the Son as poets mythologize, showing the gods to be no better than men. Rather, the Son of God is the Word of the Father in idea and activity; for through him and on account of him all things were made, the Father and the Son being one. The Son is in the Father and the Father in the Son, by unity and power of spirit; thus the Son of God is the mind and Word of the Father. If it pleases you to consider with heightened understanding what the Child intends, I will say briefly that he is the Father's firstborn, not as having been made (for God, being eternal mind, had the Word in himself from the beginning, being eternally rational), but as idea and activity proceeded, the material things having been placed underneath like a mixture of the heavier with the lighter. The prophetic spirit agrees with the Word; for it says, "The Lord created me the beginning of his ways for his works" (Proverbs 8:22). We also say that the Holy Spirit, which energizes those who speak prophetically, is an effluence of God, flowing out and returning like a ray of the sun. Who then would not be at a loss, hearing us call God the Father, God the Son, and the Holy Spirit, showing both the power of their unity and the distinction of their order, while we are called atheists? excerpts.citation: Athenagoras — Plea for the Christians (Chapter 10. The Christians Worship the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.)
excerpts.author: Athenagoras
excerpts.locus: Chapter 10. The Christians Worship the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.
excerpts.anf_chapter_title: Chapter 10. The Christians Worship the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.
english: I have shown clearly enough that we are not atheists, since we worship one God who is ungenerated, eternal, invisible, impassible, incomprehensible, and uncircumscribed. He is grasped only by mind and reason, encompassed by light, beauty, spirit, and indescribable power. Under him all things have come into being through his Word, have been adorned, and are held together. We also acknowledge the Son of God. Let no one think it laughable that the Son belongs to God. We do not conceive of him as the poets mythologize, portraying gods no better than men. Nor have we thought about God the Father or about the Son in that way. Rather, the Son of God is the Word of the Father in idea and activity. Through him and because of him all things were made, the Father and the Son being one. With the Son in the Father and the Father in the Son, by the unity and power of the Spirit, the Son of God is the mind and Word of the Father. If, in an excess of scrutiny, you press to examine what the Child means, I will state briefly: he is the firstborn of the Father, not as having been made. God, being eternal mind, has possessed the Word within himself from the beginning, being eternally rational. Instead, the Word proceeded as idea and activity before the material substances, of a divine nature, with useless earth lying beneath, mixed with the thicker parts toward the thinner upon them. The prophetic Spirit agrees with the Word, for it says, "The Lord created me the beginning of his ways for his works" (Proverbs 8:22). And we affirm that the Holy Spirit, who works in those who speak prophetically, is an effluence of God, flowing out and returning like a ray of the sun. Who would not be perplexed to hear us call ourselves worshippers of God the Father, God the Son, and the Holy Spirit — showing both their power in unity and their distinction in order — and yet be labeled atheists? Our theology does not rest on these points alone. We also confess a multitude of angels and ministers, whom the Creator and Maker of the world, God, distributed and ordered through his Word to govern the elements, the heavens, the world, all that is in it, and their good order.

excerpts.citation: Athenagoras — Plea for the Christians (Chapter 15. The Christians Distinguish God from Matter.)
excerpts.author: Athenagoras
excerpts.locus: Chapter 15. The Christians Distinguish God from Matter.
excerpts.anf_chapter_title: Chapter 15. The Christians Distinguish God from Matter.
english: Let the opponents keep their view. What follows? Since the multitude cannot distinguish matter from God, or define the boundary between them, they turn to idols made of matter. Must we who do distinguish and separate the unbegotten from the begotten, true being from non-being, the intelligible from the sensible, and assign to each its proper name, also draw near and worship statues? If matter and God are identical—two names for one reality—then by refusing to call stones, wood, gold, and silver gods we are impious. But if they are separated by an infinite distance, as far apart as the craftsman and the material he prepares for his art, what charge lies against us? Just as the potter is the craftsman and the clay is the matter, so God is the Creator and matter obeys Him for the work. Yet clay by itself cannot become vessels without the craftsman, and the all-receptive matter, apart from the Creator God, never received distinction, shape, and order. We do not value the ceramic above the potter, nor the cups and gold ornaments above the metalsmith; rather, when we praise the craftsman for the skill shown in them, he is the one who receives the glory for the vessels. Likewise, regarding matter and the ordering of adorned things, the glory and due honor belong not to matter but to its Creator, God. Therefore, if we treated the forms of matter as gods, we would show ourselves ignorant of the true God’s glory, equating the perishable and corruptible with the eternal.

Τί οὖν; Ἐπεὶ οἱ πολλοί, διακρῖναι οὐ δυνάμενοι τί μὲν ὕλη τί δὲ θεὸς πόσον δὲ τὸ διὰ μέσου αὐτῶν, προσίασι τοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ὕλης εἰδώλοις, δι᾿ ἐκείνους καὶ ἡμεῖς, οἱ διακρίνοντες καὶ χωρίζοντες τὸ ἀγένητον καὶ τὸ γενητόν, τὸ ὂν καὶ τὸ οὐκ ὄν, τὸ νοητὸν καὶ τὸ αἰσθητόν, καὶ ἑκάστῳ αὐτῶν τὸ προσῆκον ὄνομα ἀποδιδόντες, προσελευσόμεθα καὶ προσκυνήσομεν τὰ ἀγάλματα; Εἰ μὲν γὰρ ταὐτὸν ὕλη καὶ θεός, δύο ὀνόματα καθ᾿ ἑνὸς πράγματος, τοὺς λίθους καὶ τὰ ξύλα, τὸν χρυσὸν καὶ τὸν ἄργυρον οὐ νομίζοντες θεούς, ἀσεβοῦμεν. Ἀλλ᾿ ὡς ὁ πηλὸς καθ᾿ ἑαυτὸν σκεύη γενέσθαι χωρὶς τέχνης ἀδύνατος, καὶ ἡ πανδεχὴς ὕλη ἄνευ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ δημιουργοῦ διάκρισιν καὶ σχῆμα καὶ κόσμον οὐκ ἐλάμβανεν. Ὡς δὲ οὐ τὸν κέραμον προτιμότερον τοῦ ἐργασαμένου αὐτὸν ἔχομεν οὐδὲ τὰς φιάλας καὶ χρυσίδας τοῦ χαλκεύσαντος, ἀλλ᾿ εἴ τι περὶ ἐκείνας δεξιὸν κατὰ τὴν τέχνην τὸν τεχνίτην ἐπαινοῦμεν, καὶ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὴν ἐπὶ τοῖς σκεύεσι δόξαν καρπούμενος, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς ὕλης καὶ τοῦ θεοῦ τῆς διαθέσεως τῶν κεκοσμημένων οὐχ ὕλη τὴν δόξαν καὶ τὴν τιμὴν δικαίαν ἔχει ἀλλ᾿ ὁ δημιουργὸς αὐτῆς θεός. Ὥστε, εἰ τὰ εἴδη τῆς ὕλης ἄγοιμεν θεούς, ἀναισθητεῖν τοῦ ὄντος θεοῦ δόξομεν, τὰ λυτὰ καὶ φθαρτὰ τῷ ἀϊδίῳ ἐξισοῦντες.

excerpts.citation: Athenagoras — Plea for the Christians (Chapter 17. The Names of the Gods and Their Images are But of Recent Date.)
excerpts.author: Athenagoras
excerpts.locus: Chapter 17. The Names of the Gods and Their Images are But of Recent Date.
excerpts.anf_chapter_title: Chapter 17. The Names of the Gods and Their Images are But of Recent Date.
english: A defense requires precise reasoning about the names of the gods, since they are recent, and about their images, since they appeared only yesterday and the day before, so to speak. You know these facts are especially worthy of attention, because they harmonize with all ancient testimony and surpass it. I assert that Orpheus, Homer, and Hesiod are the very ones who supplied both the genealogies and the names to the gods spoken of under them. Herodotus bears witness: he judges Hesiod and Homer to be about four hundred years older than himself, and not much more; these are the poets who composed the Greek theogony, assigned the gods their epithets, distributed their honors and arts, and described their forms. As for images, they were not even thought to exist until the arts of modeling, drawing, and statue-making arose — until the time of Saurius of Samos, Craton of Sicyon, Cleanthus of Corinth, and a Corinthian maiden. Saurius invented skiagraphy by tracing a horse in sunlight; Craton invented graphic art by sketching the shadows of a man and a woman on a whitened panel; and the maiden invented coroplasty when, driven by erotic longing, she traced her lover’s shadow on a wall while he slept. Her father, a potter, delighted in the exact likeness, carved out the outline, and filled it with clay; the model is still preserved in Corinth. After them, Daedalus and Theodorus of Miletus advanced statue-making and modeling. The timespan for images and the whole business of idols is so short that one can say each craftsman is the god he fashions. The Artemis at Ephesus, the Athena — or rather Athela, since the mystics call her Athela, the ancient name derived from the olive — and the seated statue by Endoios, a pupil of Daedalus; the Pythian Apollo, a work of Theodorus and Telecleus; the Delian Apollo and Artemis, the work of Tectaeus and Angelion; the Hera in Samos and the Smilis in Argos, made by human hands; the remaining idols, the work of Phidias; the Aphrodite at Cnidus, the work of Praxiteles; the Asclepius at Epidaurus, a work of Phidias. In short, not one of them has escaped being made by a human. If they are gods, why did they not exist from the beginning? Why are they younger than their makers? Why did they need human beings and art to come into being? They are earth, stone, wood, and elaborate craftsmanship — nothing more.

Φημὶ οὖν Ὀρφέα καὶ Ὅμηρον καὶ Ἡσίοδον εἶναι τοὺς καὶ γένη καὶ ὀνόματα δόντας τοῖς ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν λεγομένοις θεοῖς. Μαρτυρεῖ δὲ καὶ Ἡρόδοτος· Ἡσίοδον γὰρ καὶ Ὅμηρον ἡλικίην τετρακοσίοις ἔτεσι δοκέω πρεσβυτέρους ἐμοῦ γενέσθαι, καὶ οὐ πλείοσι· οὗτοι δέ εἰσιν οἱ ποιήσαντες θεογονίην Ἕλλησι, καὶ τοῖσι θεοῖσι τὰς ἐπωνυμίας δόντες καὶ τιμάς τε καὶ τέχνας διελόντες, καὶ εἴδεα αὐτῶν σημήναντες. Αἱ δ᾿ εἰκόνες, μέχρι μήπω πλαστικὴ καὶ γραφικὴ καὶ ἀνδριαντοποιητικὴ ἦσαν, οὐδὲ ἐνομίζοντο, Σαυρίου δὲ τοῦ Σαμίου καὶ Κράτωνος τοῦ Σικυωνίου καὶ Κλεάνθους τοῦ Κορινθίου καὶ κόρης Κορινθίας ἐπιγενομένων· καὶ σκιαγραφίας μὲν εὑρεθείσης ὑπὸ Σαυρίου, ἵππον ἐν ἡλίῳ περιγράψαντος, γραφικῆς δὲ ὑπὸ Κράτωνος, ἐν πίνακι λελευκωμένῳ σκιὰς ἀνδρὸς καὶ γυναικὸς ἐναλείψαντος· ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς κόρης ἡ κοροπλαθικὴ εὑρέθη· ἐρωτικῶς γάρ τινος ἔχουσα περιέγραψεν αὐτοῦ κοιμωμένου ἐν τοίχῳ τὴν σκιάν, εἶθ᾿ ὁ πατήρ, ἡσθεὶς ἀπαραλλάκτῳ οὔσῃ τῇ ὁμοιότητι, (κέραμον δὲ εἰργάζετο) ἀναγλύψας τὴν περιγραφὴν πηλῷ προσανεπλήρωσεν· ὁ τύπος ἔτι καὶ νῦν ἐν Κορίνθῳ σώζεται. Τούτοις δὲ ἐπιγενόμενοι Δαίδαλος καὶ Θεόδωρος ὁ Μιλήσιος ἀνδριαντοποιητικὴν καὶ πλαστικὴν προσεξεῦρον. Ὁ μὲν δὴ χρόνος ὀλίγος τοσοῦτος ταῖς εἰκόσι καὶ τῇ περὶ τὰ εἴδωλα πραγματείᾳ, ὡς ἔχειν εἰπεῖν τὸν ἑκάστου τεχνίτην θεοῦ. Τὸ μὲν γὰρ ἐν Ἐφέσῳ τῆς Ἀρτέμιδος καὶ τὸ τῆς Ἀθηνᾶς (μᾶλλον δὲ Ἀθηλᾶς· Ἀθηλᾶ γὰρ ὡς οἱ μυστικώτερον, οὕτω γὰρ τὸ ἀπὸ τῆς ἐλαίας τὸ παλαιὸν) καὶ τὴν καθημένην Ἔνδοιος εἰργάσατο μαθητὴς Δαιδάλου, ὁ δὲ Πύθιος ἔργον Θεοδώρου καὶ Τηλεκλέους, καὶ ὁ Δήλιος καὶ ἡ Ἄρτεμις Τεκταίου καὶ Ἀγγελίωνος τέχνη, ἡ δὲ ἐν Σάμῳ Ἥρα καὶ ἐν Ἄργει Σμίλιδος χεῖρες, καὶ Φειδίου τὰ λοιπὰ εἴδωλα, ἡ Ἀφροδίτη ἐν Κνίδῳ ἑταίρα Πραξιτέλους τέχνη, ὁ ἐν Ἐπιδαύρῳ Ἀσκληπιὸς ἔργον Φειδίου. Συνελόντα φάναι, οὐδὲν αὐτῶν διαπέφευγεν τὸ μὴ ὑπ᾿ ἀνθρώπου γεγονέναι. Εἰ τοίνυν θεοί, τί οὐκ ἦσαν ἐξ ἀρχῆς; Τί δαί εἰσι νεώτεροι τῶν πεποιηκότων; Τί δαὶ ἔδει αὐτοῖς πρὸς τὸ γενέσθαι ἀνθρώπων καὶ τέχνης; Γῆ ταῦτα καὶ λίθοι καὶ ὕλη καὶ περίεργος τέχνη.

excerpts.author: Athenagoras
excerpts.locus: Chapter 18. The Gods Themselves Have Been Created, as the Poets Confess.
excerpts.anf_chapter_title: Chapter 18. The Gods Themselves Have Been Created, as the Poets Confess.
english: Some people claim that these statues are mere images, that the gods are the beings they represent, and that the honors and sacrifices offered to the images are actually transferred to those gods; they insist there is no other way to approach the gods, who appear harsh and unapproachable, and they point to the supposed miraculous powers of certain idols as proof. Let us examine, then, the power inherent in their names. Greatest Emperors, I ask you to pardon my frankness before I speak the truth; my purpose is not to accuse the idols, but, having been freed from slander, to present the reasoning behind our choice. You yourselves possess the heavenly kingdom to scrutinize; for just as all things have been entrusted to you, father and son, who received the kingdom from above — as the prophetic Spirit says, "The soul of a king is in the hand of God" — so all things have been subjected to the one God and His Word, the Son, understood as an unbroken unity. Consider this first, before all else. The gods did not exist from the beginning, as is claimed; rather, each came into being just as we are born. All their traditions agree on this. Homer says, "Ocean, the genesis of the gods, and their mother Tethys." Orpheus, who first invented their names, detailed their origins and deeds, and is regarded among them as the more truthful theologian — Homer himself follows Orpheus in most matters, especially concerning the gods — and Orpheus establishes their first origin from water: "Ocean, who has been generated as the genesis of all things." According to him, water was the beginning of all things; from water came mud, and from both was born a living dragon with a lion's head and, in the middle, a god's face, named Hercules and Chronos. This Hercules generated an enormous egg, which, filled by the force of its begetter, burst in two from friction; the upper half became heaven, the lower half earth. Then the goddess Earth emerged through a body; Heaven mingled with Earth and begot females — Clotho, Lachesis, and Atropos — and males — the hundred-handed Cottys, Gyges, and Briareus, and the Cyclopes Brontes, Steropes, and Argos. He bound them and cast them into Tartarus, having learned he would be overthrown by his own children. Consequently, Earth in anger begot the Titans. The noble Earth brought forth the heavenly youths, whom they call Titans, because they avenged great starry Heaven.

greek: Ἐπεὶ τοίνυν φασί τινες εἰκόνας μὲν εἶναι ταύτας, θεοὺς δὲ ἐφ᾿ οἷς αἱ εἰκόνες, καὶ τὰς προσόδους ἃς ταύταις προσίασι καὶ τὰς θυσίας ἐπ᾿ ἐκείνους ἀναφέρεσθαι καὶ εἰς ἐκείνους γίνεσθαι, μὴ εἶναί τε ἕτερον τρόπον τοῖς θεοῖς ἢ τοῦτον προσελθεῖν (χαλεποὶ δὲ θεοὶ φαίνεσθαι ἐναργεῖς), καὶ τοῦ ταῦθ᾿ οὕτως ἔχειν τεκμήρια παρέχουσι τὰς ἐνίων εἰδώλων ἐνεργείας, φέρε ἐξετάσωμεν τὴν ἐπὶ τοῖς ὀνόμασι δύναμιν αὐτῶν. Δεήσομαι δὲ ὑμῶν, μέγιστοι αὐτοκρατόρων, πρὸ τοῦ λόγου ἀληθεῖς παρεχομένῳ τοὺς λογισμοὺς συγγνῶναι· οὐ γὰρ προκείμενόν μοι ἐλέγχειν τὰ εἴδωλα, ἀλλὰ ἀπολυόμενος τὰς διαβολὰς λογισμὸν τῆς προαιρέσεως ἡμῶν παρέχω. Ἔχοιτε ἀφ᾿ ἑαυτῶν καὶ τὴν ἐπουράνιον βασιλείαν ἐξετάζειν· ὡς γὰρ ὑμῖν πατρὶ καὶ υἱῷ πάντα κεχείρωται, ἄνωθεν τὴν βασιλείαν εἰληφόσι (βασιλέως γὰρ ψυχὴ ἐν χειρὶ θεοῦ, φησὶ τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα), οὕτως ἑνὶ τῷ θεῷ καὶ τῷ παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ λόγῳ υἱῷ νοουμένῳ ἀμερίστῳ πάντα ὑποτέτακται. Ἐκεῖνο τοίνυν σκέψασθέ μοι πρὸ τῶν ἄλλων.Οὐκ ἐξ ἀρχῆς, ὥς φασιν, ἦσαν οἱ θεοί, ἀλλ᾿ οὕτως γέγονεν αὐτῶν ἕκαστος ὡς γινόμεθα ἡμεῖς. Καὶ τοῦτο πᾶσιν αὐτοῖς ξυμφωνεῖ· Ὁμήρου μὲν γὰρ λέγοντος· Ὠκεανόν τε, θεῶν γένεσιν, καὶ μητέρα Τηθύν, Ὀρφέως δὲ (ὃς καὶ τὰ ὀνόματα αὐτῶν πρῶτος ἐξεῦρε καὶ τὰς γενέσεις διεξῆλθε καὶ ὅσα ἑκάστοις πέπρακται εἶπε καὶ πεπίστευται παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς ἀληθέστερον θεολογεῖν, ᾧ καὶ Ὅμηρος τὰ πολλὰ καὶ περὶ θεῶν μάλιστα ἕπεται) καὶ αὐτοῦ τὴν πρώτην γένεσιν αὐτῶν ἐξ ὕδατος συνιστάντος· Ὠκεανός, ὅσπερ γένεσις πάντεσσι τέτυκται. Ἦν γὰρ ὕδωρ ἀρχὴ κατ᾿ αὐτὸν τοῖς ὅλοις, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ὕδατος ἰλὺς κατέστη, ἐκ δὲ ἑκατέρων ἐγεννήθη ζῶον δράκων προσπεφυκυῖαν ἔχων κεφαλὴν λέοντος, διὰ μέσου δὲ αὐτῶν θεοῦ πρόσωπον, ὄνομα Ἡρακλῆς καὶ Χρόνος. Οὗτος ὁ Ἡρακλῆς ἐγέννησεν ὑπερμέγεθες ὠόν, ὃ συμπληρούμενον ὑπὸ βίας τοῦ γεγεννηκότος ἐκ παρατριβῆς εἰς δύο ἐῤῥάγη· τὸ μὲν οὖν κατὰ κορυφὴν αὐτοῦ οὐρανὸς εἶναι ἐτελέσθη, τὸ δὲ κατενεχθὲν γῆ. Προῆλθε δὲ καὶ θεὸς Γῆ διὰ σώματος· Οὐρανὸς δὲ Γῇ μιχθεὶς γεννᾷ θηλείας μὲν Κλωθώ, Λάχεσιν, Ἄτροπον, ἄνδρας δὲ ἑκατόγχειρας Κόττυν, Γύγην, Βριάρεων, καὶ Κύκλωπας Βρόντην καὶ Στερόπην καὶ Ἄργον· οὓς καὶ δήσας κατεταρτάρωσεν, ἐκπεσεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν παίδων τῆς ἀρχῆς μαθών. Διὸ καὶ ὀργισθεῖσα ἡ Γῆ τοὺς Τιτᾶνας ἐγέννησε. Κούρους δ᾿ οὐρανίωνας ἐγείνατο πότνια Γαῖα, Οὓς δὴ καὶ Τιτῆνας ἐπίκλησιν καλέουσιν, Οὕνεκα τισάσθην μέγαν Οὐρανὸν ἀστερόεντα.
